column6: *0.10*After the incident, Plutonium's brain was no longer suitable for a Spark Polymer extension, *0.10*so I designed a similar Polymer-based brain function extension for him called Voskhod. Chariton, may he rest in peace, would be pleased to hear that his designs had not been wasted.

*0.10*As a young man, Plutonium, now P-3, was confident and funny, which played a key role in his assignment to Argentum. He was a promising operative, *0.10*but lagged behind many other candidates in a number of ways. However, the positive influence and infectious good humor he imparted to his fellow servicemen, *0.10*especially in comparison to the more morose Commander Kuznetsov, *0.10*served as a compelling reason to recruit him. Because of this, *0.10*the emergence of a more intimate relationship between him and Agent Blesna was only a matter of time.
Kollektiv will lead humanity to the apex of evolution, without internecine strife, without falling into the abyss of war and hatred!
The THOUGHT device can be removed, but this merely prevents the wearer from being able to make calls and give orders to machines.
Well, I'm not. I should be, but Viktor... No other outcome was possible. It... It wasn't even quite him at that point. I don't wanna talk about it.
But I... was I really married? What was my wife's name?
What were you expecting? I suspect that this room has a specific function.
What else can we do, Sergey? You and I are friends now, and we know the truth. We need to get to Sechenov, rectify this injustice, and get revenge for what he's done to us.
I work here. Well, I used to... only Sechenov can revoke my access, and he's got his hands full right now, and I'm no threat to him.
Ah, well, just you wait. Soon this is going to happen all over the Soviet Union, and later, the whole world. Then you'll see all people stripped of their free will.
Ballet and martial arts... are you trying to tell me the boss's metal twins... no way, this is total BS! The boss would never do something like that!
Oh, crap. And now it's gone...
Fuck. I don't like the sound of that.
It won't hurt, soldier. You won't even remember a thing.

*0.07*The Academy has a number of interesting departments. For example, there's the Radio of the Future. By mathematically combining short wave and quantum echoes, *0.08*we can predict the music people will be listening to fifty or even eighty years into the future. But there's another very special department here *0.08*called "Polymerized Subject Behavioral Psychology." They're supposed to be volunteers, but...
Which world is this happening in, my boy?
On Monday everyone who has undergone polymerization will become just as malleable as you.
So she hacked the system... kinda like how all these poor bastards got hacked to bits.
Right here, straight above us. Do you see it?
So that's how it is, Major. Think it over while I try to hack this elevator and get us back to the surface.
You and your wife served with the Argentum unit. Ekaterina, or "Katya," as you called her, was a highly qualified agent.
You're a good man, Comrade Major. I hate to say this, but you're the first functional example of an ordinary link in the Kollektiv network.
Where's the entry I'm supposed to play back, P-3?
What?! Sechenov has you on a leash! He does whatever he wants with you!
Just about right now. When he went offline. I had no idea Sechenov had stashed his consciousness into your glove... It was the abbreviation, "CHARLES", that tipped me off.
Crispy... I'll go get another one.

*0.06*Because Sechenov never dismisses what he can use. It's easier for him to change everything to fit his needs. *0.06*I guess you noticed this already? What's funny is that YOU seem to have made friends with your glove!

*0.10*There's nothing to explain, Major. You're just as much a CHAR-les to me as I am a perfect stranger to you. First Sechenov murdered me, then he turned me *0.09*into a blob of Polymer goo. Then he brainwashed you and manipulated you. How could I trust either of you? That's why *0.04*I pretended to be the CHatting ARtificial Librarian. I wanted to see who was who.
I only need one for now.
Wait. Charles? What data? What Voskhod polymer extension?
No thanks. A little vacation will fix me right up. I mean... if this all ends well.
This is... holy shit... fuck! That can't be...
Yeah, well... I guess I would've done the same. So what are we gonna do now, huh?
Yeah, exactly! Do you know what this shit is?
Pick any entry, Major! Time's running out!
I can't play two tapes at the same time.

*0.08*Trying to make a monkey outta me, are you? Well, join the club! Don't have any data, huh?! *0.08*You've always known about all this. There's a reason you're called CHAR-LES, right? You're CHAR-iton Zakharov, you son of a bitch! Got an explanation? Huh?!
Ekaterina. And... you aren't going to like what I'm about to tell you, Comrade Major.
Bullshit! It's just the same old chain of command, but on a virtual network. What's so awful about that?
If you worked here, then... why didn't you try to stop this?
The launch of Kollektiv is coming. We can't be late.
What are we doing here? What do you want?!
Welcome, Chariton Zakharov. What is the subject of your query today?
Atrocities? What atrocities? If they're volunteers, coming here was their choice. It's got nothing to do with me.
You know, free will doesn't guarantee that a person won't be a scumbag...
So why does Sechenov want him?
So when did you realize that Charles is Zakharov?
And they won't be able to stab each other in the back anymore. Sounds nice.

*0.10*Then science will start to flow within the minds of all the citizens of a unified nation, a great Scientific Union *0.09*that encompasses the entire globe! Kollektiv is the hand of goodness, and it is ready to embrace all mankind!
And no more grenades, or other bullshit! Any funny business at all, and I'll kill you! This is your last warning!
The test subject is not leaving Limbo. Inject neurotransmitters now!
Unfortunately, that won't help anyone. It just makes things worse.
Each book from my father's library was nothing but a fragment of the knowledge I sought.

*0.06*Of course, you're not. You were just doing your job, right? Listen, I'm sorry, but I don't want to talk about it. I loved him when he was... *0.05*Different. He was kind, understanding... And didn't kill people.
So how is Sechenov gonna keep everybody under control?
So, how do we get in?
What do you mean? I'm looking right at it!
How'd you get in here? Why didn't the Drofas stop you?
Sure. Fine. Come on, I won't waste your time.
I just don't feel comfortable around these people.
What are you even talking about? What implant?
Larisa! Crispy critters, you're around here somewhere?
Hm-m... Hallucinations are serious business. Well, I am a neurosurgeon. I can probably help—if everything ends well.
Keep it together, Major! If what I am thinking is true, I should be able to access the archive right now. There will be records about you.
Major, I... I have no data about this incident...
I am not detecting any internal changes, Major. But your Voskhod polymer extension is clearly receiving an unidentified stream of external data.
I need a bit more time here.
Everything's crystal clear to me, but you might benefit from hearing it.
Perhaps because I care? And besides, it's not about you. Well, not only you.
We are all monsters in the dark, my boy. How many times have we talked about this?
I don't see Larisa's body, so she must have gotten past the Drofas...
On himself? Was he an idiot or something?
Why would I want two tapes when I haven't even listened to one yet?
Let's give this one a spin.
They told us he ran a number of experiments... On himself. The result was disastrous and unpredictable.
Science, shattered to pieces by the husks of books no one has ever read. None of the social systems that exist now allow humanity to fully evolve. They are all flawed!
Oh, he certainly wasn't an idiot. Zakharov was a misanthrope obsessed with science. I don't think he cared about what happened to his body all that much.
I don't know. I guess he is. Except this device is based on the logical paradigm and experience of one of the brightest Soviet geniuses.
I don't know... it's like that lump of Polymer is calling out to me... a big teardrop-shaped one.

*0.07*Not really. I mean, he's never really had to, but now this whole thing with Petrov... jelly man killed Stock, and the boss didn't even bat an eye. *0.04*Is the launch of Kollektiv really so important he can't even delay it out of respect for the dead?
Not this one. I mean, it's fun and all, but still.
Long story short, your Charles is Professor Chariton Zakharov.
No data, huh? Well, I don't have any data either. So let's go get some.
I have no data on this topic, Comrade Major.
Nothing. I'm just... digesting what I saw.
But Sechenov uploaded an imprint of her professional skills into his bodyguards' matrices.
Kollektiv is a new world, a world of Limbo, a world where everyone will be intelligent and happy!
Well... we've been through a lot. I've got feelings, you know... being alive and all. And so does he.
Yeah, I already know half my body's prosthetic. What else is new?
A lighthouse, huh? And where are we supposed to look for it?
Let's take a look around. She's gotta be here.
So you're a volunteer, huh? Then why are you such a disobedient test subject?
*0.06*Procedure: implant the Voskhod Neuropolymer brain function extension. Objective: *0.06*total elimination of destructive impulses triggered by traumatic memories. Patient: Major Sergey Necheyev.
Huh, that WAS short. So how could he be Zakharov?
P-1, P-2, P-3! Your mind is never free!
Lift up your head and open your eyes, my boy. You understand the weight of a mind deprived of knowledge better than anyone else!
I believe that the unscheduled acceleration was caused by the elevator access system being hacked. Otherwise Dr. Filatova would not have been able to initiate it.
The Voskhod polymer extension was developed using data from experiments conducted by Dmitry and myself...
So Charles isn't a person anymore? Just... a device?

*0.09*Following his recovery, the agent's personality was altered significantly, including his behavioral and speech patterns. Because of this, *0.09*I made the decision to remove the agent from the Argentum unit. In order to prevent any possibility of memory recidivism, *0.09*Plutonium received a new call sign, P-3, and is now under my direct command and observation. P-3's contact with Argentum has been kept to a minimum, *0.07*and Argentum personnel have been warned against mentioning the call sign "Blesna" in P-3's presence.
After Kollektiv launches, people will be able to control robots with their minds.

*0.13*Events in Bulgaria left the agents badly injured. Technically speaking, they were clinically dead. Agent Blesna could not be saved. Since Agent Plutonium's condition was less severe, *0.10*it was possible to return him to combat readiness. However, his nearly-destroyed limbs had to be amputated and replaced with the latest prostheses.
Just look at me, Comrade Major. After I died, my consciousness was transplanted into this glove. After your wife died, her consciousness could not be saved.
Only a small bunch of people have permanent access to the Archive. Sechenov, Lebedev—the director of the Academy, and Zakharov, like you reminded me.

*0.07*Because ALL your THOUGHTs are useless! A polymerized person's signal will be transmitted to robots and other equipment *0.07*via their THOUGHT controller. But it is not what makes them a part of Kollektiv.
Cuz before, they always told me what they were doing to me... I'll go get another recording.
Professor Zakharov was developing the Kollektiv subsystems and worked on the module. The one you have inside you.
We can deal with that. Let's talk to the doc first. But if she tries to take off again, she's gonna regret it. I'm sick of playing cat and mouse with her.
Has Dr. Sechenov ever told you about his plans?

*0.09*Nechaev has emerged from his year in rehab a new man, with new habits and behaviors. For example, he's become fond of a certain euphemism... *0.09*"Crispy critters." It all started after one of the medics described him and Blesna *0.09*as "crispy critters" during his recovery. He was still in a coma at the time. He suddenly leaped out of bed and nearly strangled the medic to death. *0.10*The staff subdued him by shouting, "We're under fire!" after which Plutonium ducked for cover, hit his head, and passed out. Ever since then, *0.09*"crispy critters" has become part of his vocabulary. Could it be an example of psychological imprinting?
As a child, she studied ballet and made significant achievements in both dance and martial arts.
So... which one do you want first?
Make the world pure and great! Those who die will be preserved as digital copies. No one will ever be forgotten again!
Did Sechenov not tell you? So you don't know what is happening to you?
Listen, Doc, he saved my life. Do you think I don't know I'm a test subject? That's my job.
Just hear me out, P-3. Let me try to give you a different perspective, and then you can decide how to handle things.
*0.07*So that's Neptune, huh? Looks nice... actually, it looks amazing! A rapture! I wouldn't mind spending some time there myself... *0.04*but I can't even imagine what's going on there right now.
What do we have here? A chair and a TV? This isn't what I was expecting...
Shit... I can't let that happen... listen! That fuckin' gadget, the THOUGHT device, you can just take it off!
Oh, fuck... I'm so sick of these goddamn hallucinations!
Comrade Sechenov asked you to return to Chelomey. How will you explain this delay?
Comrade Major, this will be difficult to explain. I am...
There are lots of entries! Pick one!
Do you see colorful spots before your eyes? Does your perception of the world change?
You are a warrior of science! Take up your sword of knowledge and strike at the very heart of the capitalist bureaucracy!
How can you talk about this so calmly?
Do you know how Sechenov is planning to use Kollektiv? What he's going to do with it?

*0.10*Get rid of money and let robots toil for us! Get rid of inequality and the lie of communism. Give people freedom of choice. *0.09*Accelerate evolution! Share our knowledge with everyone and combine our minds into a single great Kollektiv!
I'm sure you would've smashed the door with your bare fists. But now Archivist thinks I am Dr. Zakharov, so got lucky. And now we can learn everything about you. Let's go.
Are we leaving, or is there anything else you want to know?
Charles! Why the fuck are you all static-y? What the hell is going on?!
Charles! Do you know what's happening with my head?
To me, Chariton Radeonovich died a long time ago. I am done mourning him. And besides, I'm a scientist, we're more impassionate towards death than to muddling one's brains.
Fluffy, huh? Ha ha... so what would we have done if the password hadn't worked?
That's enough. I'm too busy to chat right now.
Do you want to search for something else?
It's a Chatting Artificial Librarian, an AI in my polymer glove. it doesn't matter. Charles, what are you talking about?!

*0.07*It's the Neuropolymer injection that makes people part of Kollektiv. It embeds itself in the brain and connects it to the neural network *0.08*once and for all. The effect of this injection cannot be undone. Everyone who gets an injection will be part of Kollektiv forever.
What? "Yourself?" And why are you calling Dr. Sechenov "Dmitry?" Who are you?
I guess you're right, Chariton—justice does need to be done...
What's that interface? Who are you talking to?
What? Did you have no choice? You couldn't have acted differently? Will you now tell me that you are sorry? What?!
We've got a ride, Major. We can get out of here!

*0.06*This is the Academy of Consequences, the Facility's memory, analytics center, and primary archive. *0.05*The activities of all the other complexes are studied here in order to draw conclusions and generate probability matrices.
This is a hallucinatory reaction, a side effect of the surgery you underwent. The reaction of a damaged brain to the presence of a neuropolymer implant.
These are just general observations. Find another recording.

*0.08*That book is about human greed and human evil. People have no time to dedicate themselves to science. On the other side of the world, *0.08*they're busy playing with money, and on this side, they're playing with the power of the masses.
You were crossing into Limbo, but it can't be stopped! How did you interrupt it?!

*0.07*I thought it was for the best. I thought it was for the good of the entire Soviet Union. But when I realized what was really going on... *0.06*I had to bide my time, wait for the right moment. Viktor and I risked everything, and... you know the rest...

*0.07*I've spent my entire life putting those fragments back together, juxtaposing each scientific fact, *0.07*and once I'd completed the puzzle, I found a book that now prevents me from sharing my knowledge with the world.
I'm waiting for a recording, Major.
I do not detect anyone in the vicinity.
I don't trust anyone. But she's got something important to tell me. And I'm sure Dr. Sechenov is hiding something.
I'm fine. My head's been killing me lately. I've been seeing things. This is one hell of a job, let me tell you...

*0.10*I used to think that way too. But that's not how things really are. Kollektiv isn't just about controlling robots. Sechenov will be able *0.05*to control everyone who's a part of Kollektiv. Kollektiv is diabolical, Nyichaev! It's even worse than slavery!
I've heard that before. But I doubt anything could surprise me now.
Citizens! Collect your thoughts and connect your THOUGHT!

*0.10*On behalf of all of Facility 3826, I present to you the device of the future: the neural connector THOUGHT. *0.09*It will allow human beings to be at the center of Kollektiv 2.0, a network for all mankind together, *0.08*uniting the intellects of all individuals into a powerful mind free of all boundaries!

*0.09*Comrade! As a citizen of the mighty Soviet Union, join your compatriots and undergo polymerization today! Stand with Kollektiv 2.0! *0.07*Learn how to control robots with your own mind! Explore space! Reach the pinnacle of evolution! *0.10*The global launch of Kollektiv 2.0, our marvelous network, will be on the 13th day of the month of June, 1955, only two days away! *0.10*Get your THOUGHT device today, and become Homo Futurum among the first! The future is already yours!

*0.11*Undergo polymerization! Wear your THOUGHT device! Become part of Kollektiv 2.0! Master unprecedented abilities and revolutionize what your mind is capable of! *0.07*A new era in the history of mankind is coming. Be one of the first to join the new future!

*0.05*Thanks to my invention of Neuropolymers and the process of mimetic adaptation, *0.08*it has now become possible to launch a world-wide, all-encompassing version of the Kollektiv 2.0 network. *0.04*At last: a network of humans and robots! *0.04*Humans will be able to control machines with their thoughts alone. *0.08*And, finally, we will be free to forget the difficult, tedious drudgery of unskilled labor and dedicate ourselves to science!

*0.10*Greetings, comrades. I am Dmitry Sechenov, and this is Facility 3826. A warm welcome to your future! Today we stand on the brink of the greatest event in the history of mankind. *0.10*We find ourselves just a step away from amazing evolutionary victory that will profoundly change the world as we know it. No, I'm not exaggerating! *0.07*Just look at how our beloved Soviet Union has been transformed in the last few decades!

*0.10*Your potential will be unlimited! Want to learn a foreign language in a minute? Master quantum physics in a day? Memorize literary masterpieces from around the world? *0.06*This all will be possible once your THOUGHT neural connector is installed right here on your temple. *0.10*All communication between your brain and your personal THOUGHT device is made possible via a tiny injection of Neuropolymer at a local center for Polymerization, *0.09*where you will also receive your THOUGHT device. In five minutes—in just five minutes!—you'll become the future.

*0.08*Any citizen of the USSR can obtain a THOUGHT device for free! But it gets even better: here, in our beloved Chelomey Complex, you can start using your THOUGHT device right now, *0.08*two full days ahead of the official launch of the Kollektiv 2.0 global network!

*0.05*Thanks to the THOUGHT neural connector, you will control robots with your mind, *0.09*mastering academic subjects with breathtaking speed, accessing all human knowledge, and, of course, combining it with your own individual discoveries! *0.08*You will no longer need control panels, cumbersome communications equipment and loudspeakers, documents, electronic notebooks, etc. *0.04*THOUGHT will replace every single one of all, and so much more!

*0.10*Armed with a stylish, eye-catching THOUGHT Neural Connector, you will no longer have to lug around unwieldy radiotelephones, bulky cameras, barometers, thermometers, or compasses. *0.10*This portable device will even double as an incredibly useful headlight. Its light will always be directed at what you are actually looking at. And the best part is that *0.10*changing its direction requires no other input, save for a single mental command. That's right! The THOUGHT device works as a neural interface, connecting its user *0.08*to the global Kollektiv 2.0 network, where everything is controlled by the power of thought.

*0.09*The THOUGHT Neural Connector is Facility 3826's newest R&D product, the brainchild of an elite cadre of Soviet scientists and engineers working at the forefront *0.09*of multidisciplinary science and technology. This device is set to completely revolutionize the world. Armed with a THOUGHT device, in just two days, any polymerized Soviet citizen *0.11*will be able to learn to control robots with the power of their mind. The world will never be the same again!

*0.09*Not just an indispensable piece of hardware, the THOUGHT device is also a stylish personalized gadget. It combines high-tech, user-friendly digital solutions with an elegant, *0.09*eye-pleasing look in a wide range of colors. You can find a THOUGHT device that matches your eye color, your favorite dress, or anything you like! *0.05*With a THOUGHT device, the world around you will never be dull again!
Dear Lyudmila, I'd like to inform you that... No, no, that's too official. This isn't a formal letter, dammit...
Major! The Drofa is initiating combat maneuvers!
Lyudmila, my dearest, words cannot express how I... No, it's too sappy. What are you, a schoolboy? Ugh, why is this so bloody difficult?
Heart of the Robot: a Peaceful Atom.
We've got plenty of THOUGHT devices. There won't be a shortage, said People's Deputy Alexander Shalchinov in response to widespread concern in the city of Ozyorsk.
THOUGHT—one small device for the consumer, one giant leap for mankind.
I loved you once, and love, it may well be,—or, maybe, headache—drills my brain with glee... Argh! I can't put this into words! Can't I just send her my feelings?
But what will the difference be, exactly?
But what do you think it's about, Semyon?
Yeah. Can you imagine what things will be like a year from now? Or fifty?
Yes, but also perfect execution and impeccable technique!

*0.10*And the level of detail is also amazing! You can see EVERYTHING. Every thread in the fabric, every pore, every crease and wrinkle—it's all there! *0.09*I'm 100% positive that a human craftsman could never have achieved this. Not even now! Am I right, Ellie?
Actually... is there still time to go get it?
You think I'd look good with a goatee, Ellochka?
What am I supposed to do about it?! What the...
Whatever that guy's been smoking, sign me up.
I wonder if they could make a robot dog... like a real one, except you don't need to take it to a vet, and it won't get old...
Everything's up and running in Chelomey. There are some restrictions, but you can already control robots!
They use them to deliver the mail. It's like I'm in a children's book!
Have you been to the laboratory? They've even got an open-air planetarium there!
Hey, Slavka! Today's your birthday, right? And you thought I'd forget? I never forget. Never.
Have you seen the engineer? Hilarious!
You're awfully cynical for a gizmo, ya know that? Cartoons kick ass!
I'm the Worker? I wanna be the Cosmonaut!
So, what's going on in biology right now?
You know what? That's actually a great idea!
That, my friend, you must check out for yourself. I highly recommend it. It's truly amazing. Just don't tell anyone about it until after you've been.
The moment they connect me to Kollektiv, I'm studying astrophysics. All of it. And chemistry. And math.
I'll be the Cosmonaut, so keep still!
Heh, I can still remember how it all started. You know, the first robots couldn't even walk! The very first model—back in '39—had wheels and a cable THIS long.
Absolutely! Allow me to connect you.
The vehicle is waiting downstairs. You should hurry, you don't have much time.
Or making sandwiches without lifting a finger!
Dr. Sechenov is far from your average scientist.
Look at that, Alexander! This is what the future looks like!
Hi, I'm looking for Mr. Jazz, first name Hugh. Is he there?
Hi, do you have Prince Albert in a can?
If I had a ruble for every time I've been asked that question, I'd be a capitalist. But I hope that very soon we will fly to the stars and become aliens to other races.
I can't wait! Going to the stars is my dream. No one has even been there before. We could be the first!
Sailor or astronomer—with a THOUGHT device, you can train for any profession in no time!

*0.10*Great news for our starving African comrades! The famine that has ravaged the African republics for the last two decades is all but eliminated. *0.12*The Academy of Sciences estimates that, thanks to the Vavilov Complex's breakthroughs in the cultivation of various crops, Africa will produce 120% of the food it needs next year.
Thanks a lot, but I've gotta go.
At the moment, the device functions as a personal telephone set and headlight, but it also allows the user to get used to wearing it on their head.
A sound mind needs a sound body. You look young for your age.
Very well. The laboratory is running smoothly, and my thesis is progressing nicely. You?
You'll see how special I am soon enough. But you are to refer to me as CHAR-les, the CHatting ARtificial Librarian and Educational System.
In our age of scientific breakthroughs, age is just a number.
In the blink of an eye, power-hungry dictators had turned the civilized world into a raging inferno, a tragedy that will forever be remembered in every nation and every household.

*0.12*A memorial mound called the Memorial to the Great has been erected in Moscow to commemorate all the men of science who have sacrificed their lives for the sake of knowledge, *0.12*from the obscure Dark Ages to the recent upheaval of the Brown Plague. This morning General Secretary Khrushchev addressed the nation at the unveiling of the Memorial.
Vadim, Vadim! Did you see that?
I say this is a historic spot. A nation should know its past.
Get your rusty metal asses outta here!
Didn't your mother ever teach you not to walk up to strangers and invade their personal space?
Don't you think that may have been a bit too much?

*0.07*You don't like it? We analyzed dozens of drawings made by various Komsomol art instructors in order to imitate the style. *0.05*Please point out what exactly is not to your liking, and we will amend our practice in the future.
You like it? They were made by robots for this festive occasion.
This is Facility 3826's audio guide. We will soon be arriving at our destination. Estimated time of arrival is 11:47 AM. Outside temperature: +26°C. There is a slight breeze.
Which yet survive, stamped on these lifeless things,  The hand that mocked them and the heart that fed:
And up! And turn! And right! And left! Snappier now! Just a few more!
Yeah, it was all worth it.
The entire Soviet Union is ecstatic about the unveiling of Kollektiv 2.0. with parades in every city!
You have our eternal gratitude, my friends. Thank you.
See? The devil is in the detail—or, in this case, the beard. You dismiss human genius, but it's the small imperfections that make it art.
Viktoria, get over here, quick! Look at that!
The American government is expressing deepening concern about the skyrocketing unemployment figures following the deliveries of robotic workers from the Soviet Union.
This Rafik is a real Jack-of-all-trades!
They made it a national holiday! If only I could work here... I'd never ask for a day off! This city is amazing!
Yeah, on the Kondor. One time some genius like you forgot to put up a fence. But those cows only flew in one direction: straight down.
A philosophical question but if you're asking about technology, we'll have it in a couple of years. But whether we're truly ready for it, every person has to make up their own mind.
You know, I'd like to drive a rocket to Sirius.
Everything up to there should be in the picture! It'll look great.
Wait until they're all running on electricity—that'll be something!
A decade ago, I'd never have believed things like this were possible.
I don't get it... we'll all have equal rights? What about "to each according to his ability?"
That's right, Vova. Never forget. Never forget anyone!
And I left my camera at home. Imagine that!
Whoa, what a gag! I remember that one!
Talk about style! Science is power, I tell ya. The boss has a way of looking down on insurmountable obstacles. I really respect that.
Alright, everything's set. Hold on, I forgot to lock up...
Still chugging along, crunching the old numbers. PTA-6 is interesting. I bet there's a bunch of improvements we can make to the armor.
When you really think about it, today's festivities are a celebration of every Facility employee's personal achievement.
I wish I could just chill out and watch cartoons all day... instead of dealing with this crap.
Oh, come on, time's running out!
Whatever you like! Everything will be possible!
Everything the light touches... is our Facility!

Pull yourself together. You have to follow this path first!
Well, the Kollektiv hasn't been launched yet. Technically, neither has the Atomic Heart project. So we have time to get out of here. Time for you to move!
Anyway, I'm not just a piece of polymer!
Now. These lovely things are a projection of your ego. It's like if someone was rude to you, and you said nothing, but then you're up half the night thinking about how you should have responded.
You'll figure out what to do here quickly. Not easy-peasy, but we have to defeat everyone.
Your ego's fighting against you and your sense of universal injustice!
Technically, you're fighting with yourself. Youthful maximalism. Ha! Classic!
What you're struggling with is Limbo's natural reaction to your ego, and vice versa... Okay, deal with that first.
You're closer to the source of consciousness!
Ha! Even Comrade Muravyova! Granny Zina. I wish I could forget all of this with you and start living a normal life. We have a plan and a chance!
Ha ha! Don't pout. I'm just glad I can finally talk to you!

I want to ask you something. When you get out of Limbo, please find what remains of the robot Twin and find the rings you had to throw away. We can use them to disappear from the Kollektiv's sight forever.
I haven't seen anything like that before! What does he want from us?!
This'll be the last round. Mark my words!
I'd hoped Comrade Gingerbread Man was finished and we could forget about him.
I definitely spoke too soon! Hit him, Sergey, don't stop!
I'll try to negotiate with him. Varlon tabutah chok! That didn't work? Weird...
Have I already told you how time moves here?

Although he has no interest whatsoever in the theater, Papkin knows robots and complex technological processes like the back of his hand. An introvert, he prefers to work at night in order to avoid his coworkers. He is a heavy smoker, which has led to a great deal of conflict with the performers, who often complain about the acrid stench of his cheap tobacco.

The BEA-Ds autonomous magnetons proved to be a decisive factor. After I switched the BEA-Ds into autonomous combat mode, they successfully evade NORA's manipulators and the neural puppets. Colonel Muravyova continues her efforts to use the neural puppet to catch the BEA-Ds, but so far, she has neither been able to seize the carriers, nor get them to destroy their cargo or self-destruct. The magnetons are not responding to the hub's commands. However, in my favor, the Mendeleev Complex has dozens of BEA-D robots whose specifications perfectly match the carriers. The bodies of the carriers I used have individual markings and different color, but they managed to disappear in this crowd of identical magnetons roaming aimlessly about the Mendeleev Complex. I'm thinking about how to search out and collect the carriers manually. I have no solution at present.

An agronomist and food service engineer, Zolotukhin was one of the first to speak out against Lysenko and his theory before Vavilov's theories had been approved. A businesslike man of few words, he has demonstrated a high level of professionalism when it comes to overseeing the activities of the complex.

Dr. Sechenov is a neurosurgeon, roboticist, inventor, and philanthropist. He began his career studying collective intelligence at the Soviet Academy of Medical Sciences' Brain Research Center, where he hoped to engineer a perfect way of life for the communal cities of the future. He worked on the ManKind Project before the war, but dedicated himself to studying the Polymer after it was discovered. After World War II he was put in charge of a robotics program designed to make up for the country's significant lack of human resources and took over Facility 3826 on Comrade Stalin's personal order. Once Soviet robots had been distributed throughout the world, Comrade Sechenov become the Minister of Industry. His revolutionary discovery of the Polymer's capacity for mimetic adaption made it possible to inject this extraordinarily promising new technology into human tissues. This laid the framework for what would later become Kollektiv 2.0, a merging of humans and machines into a single neural network capable of fundamentally transforming and improving the everyday lives of not just Soviet citizens, but the entire world.

Zakharov was Sechenov's best friend and colleague (although many have remarked that the scientists were bound more by a strong professional relationship than anything else, and no one ever saw any evidence of real friendship between them). He worked with him on most of his innovations, starting before the war and ending with the discovery of the Neuropolymer. Unlike Sechenov, Zakharov was introverted and antisocial. Journalists and colleagues have emphasized that while Sechenov was driven by a desire to help mankind, Zakharov only seemed to derive pleasure from learning the laws of the universe and subjugating them to his intellect. Unfortunately, his misanthropy and indifference to his own well-being led him to ignore safety protocols, and he was killed during one of his own experiments.

During their year and a half at the Academy, these twin brothers have become its unspoken symbol. Despite their lackadaisical attitude, excessive frivolity, and constant jibes at their coworkers' expense, the Klimovs are skilled specialists who have made a number of improvements to the statistics-gathering process that vastly increased its efficiency. However, they told no one about this for the first two months, preferring to spend their newfound free time on video games designed to look like work software.

A former regional war commissar in the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic, Mukhtarev was assigned to Vavilov Complex following his early retirement due to an accident. According to his fellow servicemen and subordinates, not even the robots and architects know every inch of the complex as well as he does.

As the village overseer, Abdurakhimov routinely plans leisure and practical activities for employees lodged in Forester Village. He is extremely responsible and scrupulous, but has been prosecuted for embezzlement in the past. Because of this, he is extremely quick to curtail any attempt to use resources for anything other than their officially designated purpose.
Need a vacation? Go to China!

Formerly prima ballerina Ryzhova's best friend, now a soloist at the Maya Plisetskaya Theater, Tamara Artemenkova had had to fill in for her ex-friend in lead roles when the latter was unable to make it to a performance (primarily due to capriciousness and a refusal to share the stage with robots, of course). Despite the enormous competition between human and robot ballerinas, Artemenkova loves and respects her mechanical colleagues and proudly boasts about sharing the stage with them, seeing it as an unprecedented artistic experiment.

A WWII veteran who lost his leg in the war and experienced extreme PTSD as a result. He has a very negative attitude toward robots, colleagues who sympathize with his disability, and prisoners sentenced to community service. He is unsociable and rude, but regularly receives recognition for his tireless dedication to duty, which he uses to prove over and over again to himself and others that he is still fit for work.

Ismailov is a war veteran and retired officer. He is a gruff, straightforward, and crude man with an excellent reputation as a security expert. His obvious character flaws include a tendency to promote his friends, especially those who served with him in the military, which often leads to conflict with the VDNH's other managers.

Despite his parents' and teachers' expectations, Petelka did not become a famous physicist. Although he certainly had the potential, the young man's exceptional mind and fantastic imagination ultimately allowed his reach to exceed his grasp. Comrade Petelka learned about robots from a newspaper article even before the war and never stopped fantasizing about them. Petelka did end up becoming a physicist, although he was never famous. He worked with Comrade Filimonenko on a cold Polymer synthesis project, was an excellent robot configuration technician at the Maya Plisetskaya Theater, and even made his way to the secret departments of the AoC, where he truly felt his "insignificance before the vastness of the cosmos."  "I understand this world perfectly. We're all just grains of sand in an ocean of electrical connections," Comrade Petelka declared before retiring from science, effective immediately. But he did not leave the Facility. Having returned to his duties configuring robots and servicing the theater's electrical grid, Petelka is, perhaps more than any other Soviet citizen, eagerly anticipating the Kollektiv 2,0 update that will utterly efface the boundary between human cognition and the capabilities of robots.  "We're all just electric currents, just ones and zeroes" is a favorite phrase of Petelka's, who often spends his free time in the theater's coat check room observing his favorite robot, the coat check girl.

Everything is worse than I expected. Lacking the proper expertise, the traitor Petrov attempted a second-rate, primitive hack on NORA. He not only failed to subdue her brain, but also triggered an unbounded aggravation of the dangerous pathologies he injected into her control algorithms. NORA is out of control, highly aggressive, and gripped by extremely unhealthy delusions arising from the aforementioned pathologies. Her brain's aggression continues to intensify. I am looking for a solution to the problem.

A top-notch neurosurgeon and colleague of Zakharov's, Dr. Filatova is a talented Academy employee and a specialist known for her intelligence and subtly manipulative behavior. After her mentor's death, she continued to work on integrating human consciousness into the Kollektiv 2.0 network. Her social rating has been reduced due to her romantic relationship with Viktor Petrov.

As a child in the hot city of Koktebel, Alexei Kasitsyn quickly developed a passion for the work of Russian botanist Ivan Michurin, even breeding an enormous ear of corn to the delight of his compatriots. His amazing creation can still be observed at the Facility 3826 VDNH today. After being awarded a medal of honor by Comrade Khrushchev, Junior Lab Assistant Kasitsyn took a brief vacation and returned to his hometown before taking charge of a new secret project in a more senior role.
State Television and Radio of the USSR

Date: June 1, 1955 From: Concierge G. Karpenko To: Chemistry Department Junior Lab Tech K. Litvinski  Ksenia! Please don't take this as arrogance or rudeness—but I find myself powerless! Since the day you crossed the threshold of our hotel, I've not been able to forget you! As soon as my eyes close, I see the line of your brows, your captivating bright smile, shapely figure, and delicate fingers! I'm sure you get hundreds of notes like this every day and this humble message from your admirer will get lost among them, like tears in the rain. But, Ksenia, you are beautiful! My life is a dream of you, and I dream of a date with great anticipation!

Date: June 1, 1955 From: Chemistry Department Junior Lab Tech K. Litvinski To: Junior Lab Tech E. Basinskaya  Katya, he wrote to me! That concierge, remember? The blond one, gorgeous like Apollo. Oh, his writing—I blushed all over while I read it. Nobody has ever spoken to me like that before. I remember you forbade me from dating colleagues, but he isn't a colleague or even a scientist. Katya, I'm going to try to find my happiness. I'm still all alone. I eat halva, I eat spice cake, but I can't seem to taste true love.

Are we creating new life or cloning humans here? Why the piety for a stream of electrons and polymeric microcircuits? How am I to understand this order?

Date: June 2, 1955 From: #notification_service To: #pears_lyogkaya  Vanya, get this propaganda sales pitch out to all the terminals at the Lyogkaya. We need to sell another 50 tickets fast! Many of our compatriots are missing out on China's beauties, preferring Bulgaria, Turkey, or Czechoslovakia! But the Celestial Empire is where you can see thousands-years of history mingled with the triumph of socialism, as well as deserts and jungles, and wonders of the world and nature! And all that for just 30 rubles! Direct any questions to: [Vanya, insert the accounting department's phone number here—I don't remember it].

Date: June 2, 1955 From: Chemistry Department Junior Lab Tech K. Litvinski To: Concierge G. Karpenko  Dear Gleb! I am extremely flattered and taken by your love confession and your style! That said, I am a scientist, not a poet. Writing long, flowery texts is beyond me. So I'm going to write plainly—our feelings are mutual! I have just one request—don't try to impress me. I'm a simple girl from a workers' and peasants' family. Let's just be ourselves! P.S. Now you can ask me on a date!

Date: June 3, 1955 From: Maintenance Dept. Manager N. Larionov To: Junior Lab Tech E. Basinskaya  Katya, excellent news! Do you remember Zakirov and Gaivoronsky? We traveled together to a symposium about semiconductor lasers in Egypt. They're still enamored by the local hookahs. So, they've created homemade hookahs from canisters and retort pouches! And now they're inviting people to light up. Of course, they don't let in youngsters... after all, damaging one's health should be a conscious choice... But their mixtures are so rich and aromatic—you'll love it! They've evidently made friends with one of our chemists—so, so smooth! P.S. They don't have anything to do with White and Pinker. I know you'd disapprove if they did. P.P.S. Swing by the Lyogkaya Hotel today. You want the door with the red cross.

Date: June 4, 1955 From: Concierge G. Karpenko To: #hotel_staff  Comrades! We're starting a fun little game. As you know, several of our guests find it terribly funny that our hotel sign starts with "He". They'll often call to book a room and, in a low-pitched voice, introduce themselves as Mr. Lium. When the concierge asks for the first name, lo and behold, they reply: "He!" — "He who?" — "HeLium!" It's so hilarious that everybody is already tired of it. Sometimes we get dozens of these prank calls in a month, sometimes not one. Anyway, Vasya thought of some great fun—for a month, we'll tally up the comedians and those who act normal. At the end of the month, we'll all put in 5 kopecks and place bets. Please, please don't cheat and don't egg on guests or management. Of course, don't say a word about our kitty! P.S. I think that Vasya, who came up with this idea, is a true HeNius!

Date: June 4, 1955 From: Facility 3826 Director D. Sechenov To: AoC Director A. Lebedev  The Facility will expand in the future. That's obvious and inevitable. The time has come to think about new complexes associated with not only technology and medicine, but also culture. I know you, like most scientists, think humanities folks are inferior, but let me point out your fundamental error. I will never forget how sci-fi books inspired me as a child. Note that none of our technologically advanced science would exist if not for the romantics and dreamers. Physics, chemistry, and neurobiology are wonderful, of course. But there's no point in uncovering the mysteries of the universe without a host of talented troubadours to extol these triumphs.

Date: June 5, 1955 From: Lyogkaya Hotel Office Manager E. Sobol To: Maintenance Dept. Manager N. Larionov  I'm afraid I'll fall through! Dear repairmen! Would you urgently take care of the floor in one of our (closed) buildings? Some sort of mold has chewed up the floor surface, leaving a hole so big even a cabinet could fall through. One guest has already lost a suitcase after accidentally dropping it. I'm glad we don't have thieves anymore, because anyone could climb through that hole. Please fix this as soon as possible.

Date: June 5, 1955 From: Concierge G. Karpenko To: Chemistry Department Junior Lab Tech K. Litvinski  I'm an old soldier and don't know the words of love, but let me say this, Ksenia: do you want a relationship that is vast but pure? Then come to the hay barn when it gets dark. Will you?

Date: June 7, 1955 From: Head of the Explosive Reactions Department D. Turchinsky To: #mendeleev_staff  Dear colleagues! Comrade Shalchinov, People's Deputy of Ozyorsk city, set up a Three Heroes 1.6.1 gaming tournament on the intranet. Anybody with a social rating over 7.5 can participate! Three trips to the PRC will be awarded to the lucky winners.

Date: June 7, 1955 From: Junior Chemical Handler Arthur Klarkov To: Junior Chemical Handler Samuel Shklovsky  Why are we furiously tearing through space? What are we looking for? I ask, but it's clear as day. There are two possibilities: either we are alone in the Universe or we are not. Both prospects are equally horrible. If we die alone, that isn't so bad. But if... What am I getting at? I have bad news. It seems that something has been found in the new Martian soil samples. And that means we haven't passed through the "Great Filter" yet and that after flying into deep space everything could still go to shit...

Date: June 7, 1955 From: Junior Lab Tech E. Basinskaya To: Junior Lab Tech V. Vapovich  Have you ever wondered what this hookah of yours is? It's an atomizer! You break up this vape juice, the glycerin, sugar—what's in there? Splitting it into atoms! Take a look at the smoke through the sunlight—it's floating grit! Coal, all kinds of organic chemicals, and you're pushing all of those particles into your lungs. You and I are chemists. We know that the body, which is made of bricks, is altogether fragile. We shouldn't bombard it with unnatural cobblestones.

Date: June 7, 1955 From: AoC Director A. Lebedev To: #personal_notes  We currently name complexes in honor of the outstanding scientists of the past and present: Mendeleev, Pavlov, Vavilov... But what will we do in the future? Will the Facility have new complexes dedicated to what we consider impossible now? Teleportation, time control, manipulation of gravity? What will the complexes of the future be called? Will they take the names of geniuses raised by the Kollektiv? Or will we simply call them something like Teleportation Complex? Or perhaps they won't have names, because the Facility itself will become unnecessary as all mankind transforms into a scientific community? I want to see the future, but right now, for the future's sake, I need to seriously engage with the present.

Date: April 1, 1955 From: Lyogkaya Hotel Manager S. Bodrov To: #hotel_staff  Comrade coworkers! I remind you that alcohol is forbidden! What's this debauchery at night? Have you started serving liquor again? What will you say when some Icarus, inspired by a little vodka, is dangling from a flying bridge?! Immediately remove all bar paraphernalia from the cafeterias! Suppress the dispensing of vodka. Set all the drunks straight! Everything must be in order!

Date: September 1, 1955 From: Lab Assistant Gromov Z. K. To: #mendeleev_techmaintenance  Please double-check and, if necessary, calibrate the DOC in Medical Building 4. I asked for a vial with 400 drops of valerian, but he dispensed 402! That's money down the drain, since it doesn't match with the receiving system! Figure this out. It's annoying.

Date: July 10, 1954 From: Secretary O. Dvortsova To: #bulletin_board_archive  I was thinking about the difference between worldviews and naming schemes. If robots had been invented in, say, the US and not in the USSR, then what names and designations would they have? Take Vova. Who would he be in America? For some reason, I think they would call him Nik, short for Nikola Tesla. Well, why not? Genius, visionary, talent, misanthrope. Oh, and nothing would even need to change: the moustache would stay. But an American Nik would probably have hair. And the robot would more likely be Austrian.

Date: May 11, 1952 From: Secretary O. Dvortsova To: Senior Programmer of the Logic Department E. Amperyan  Edik, I'm afraid... Now I started singing this lullaby all the time about being "nipped on the tum." After our walk and the stories of AI, I started chatting with the repair vendor every day. At first, she asked simple and dumb questions. It was cute. But then things got worse and worse. She asked me who would I choose if one of my parents must abandon me, and today she even asked whether I would eat my dog if I was starving to death... This doesn't seem normal to me, Edik. Is there a way to turn her off? You've always said that AI should have a circuit breaker, right?

Date: May 11, 1955 From: Physics and Chemistry Professor A. Kheimsov To: Secretary O. Dvortsova  Oksana! I heard your report about Mendeleev's involvement in the space program. What did you mean by this? "Including our chemists' modest contribution." Modest contribution?! Without us, they would have produced the first spaceship based on 164 tons of pyroxylin! The fact that we're all here at the Facility means we're part of something magnificent! You, me, Sechenov, and Lebedev—we are all equally accomplished! Even arguing this is ill-advised. Never underestimate your achievements!

Date: January 11, 1955 From: Director of Research Lab No. RE-5 A. Weskervich To: Academic Secretary V. Birkin  Vasily! Excellent work on Monday. Who would have thought that old man Markov really did still have a handle on bioengineering? Here I was thinking those precious leeches of his, which he experiments on so diligently, had scrambled his brains. Anyway, here's why I'm writing: what do you think, should we push the top brass regarding the report on chemical mutagens? You saw my latest experiments. Mutated RNA of the UR-0C virus could start a new revolution, especially right now, while polymers rule the world. You be the judge: we could take our experiments to an entirely new level, conduct trials not on a few vagrants and rats, but on... villages and cities! Just imagine: complete global saturation with the virus. It needs air and space to expand. I'm sure you understand.

Date: January 12, 1955 From: Director of Research Lab No. RE-5 A. Weskervich To: Academic Secretary V. Birkin  That makes sense, Vasya. Then it's settled: abandon large-scale experiments and concentrate on pressing tasks. Say hi to Anna for me. See you at bingo on Friday (I hope you didn't forget).

Date: January 12, 1955 From: Academic Secretary V. Birkin To: Director of Research Lab No. RE-5 A. Weskervich  I hope you sent that message over a secure line, Albert, otherwise you and I are in deep trouble. Are you serious? Where would we squeeze in with our papers when the second Kollektiv launch is just around the corner? Who cares about us now? And most importantly, who will give us permission to conduct research if nothing short of the whole country has already been reserved for the biggest experiment? Let's at least wait until all the hype surrounding THOUGHTs and Kollektivs has passed, and then maybe we can request something. As you know, I'm going to get back to work. Markov's leeches will devour me if I don't give them injections in time. Over and out.

Date: June 13, 1955 From: Head of the Explosive Reactions Department D. Turchinsky To: #bulletin_board_archive  Disabled combat robots were removed from Sakhalin today. It is unclear when they will return to service and whether they are needed now. In the event of a hypothetical war, we have enough tanks, bombers, and artillery. And after such a shock, such horror, people only want peace, at any price... Now I understand how Oppenheimer felt. Disgusting.

Date: April 15, 1955 From: Head of the Ecosystems Department I. Baver To: Maintenance Dept. Manager N. Larionov  I'm writing in a muddled state. My head hasn't been right since last night. Anyway, International Day of the Mushroom is celebrated on April 16. Why is it so important? This is still a young theory, but if the Earth's atmosphere warms by two or three degrees... In short, fungus is the true ruler of the planet. And mycology is very important for studying this uncontrollable power. P.S. Understand that fungus isn't simply among us. It may become some of us. Or even the last of us. P.P.S. In one of the rooms, I gathered specimens of parasitic fungi. We've got to know our enemy, so I'm asking you to not report this violation for now!

Date: June 15, 1955 From: DATA DELETED To: DATA DELETED  I am aware of the order to leave Comrade Sivukhin alone, but after the launch of Kollektiv 2.0 I did take a look at his presence in the system. According to the new protocols for tracking people... there is no trace of him in the Kollektiv. As only two days have passed, this is not currently a critical issue, but I had a duty to report.

Date: June 15, 1955 From: Office Manager Ivanov To: Maintenance Dept. Manager N. Larionov  listen, what do you want from me? why should I keep working? i heard that 87% of people who connect to the kollektiv increase their activity and enhance their qualifications. but what did sechenov tell us? that the kollektiv would come and everybody would relax while robots work. well, i want to spend all my days using pear and thought! its my right not everyone goes big brain. i spent so many years at work so i could do nothing later so you cant call me lazy! laziness is the engine of progress! Ps: not an exam so no need to worry about grammar in dms!!!

Date: June 15, 1955 From: AoC Director A. Privalov To: Physics and Chemistry Professor A. Kheimsov  I'll get straight to the point. As you know, in the aftermath of the events at the AoC, we face an extreme shortage of fresh, well-trained, and talented employees. Your chemists at Mendeleev produce stunning results, as if you're injecting talent straight into their brains instead of training them. Please select your ten most competent personnel and transfer them to us at the Academy of Consequences. I genuinely understand the displeasure this request may cause, but we're all working toward the same goal, and your help is crucial to me in light of the grave condition of my health after the robot attack.

Date: June 15, 1955 From: AoC Director A. Lebedev To: #bulletin_board_archive  After Project USSR was officially terminated and our planet confidently started down the path of the Kollektiv Republic, I've become more and more convinced that the ideas of the old world were stupid. And the most stupid of them was the war, or pre-war confrontation between the US and the USSR. The Earth and all humanity comprise an enormous body, a biosphere, an organism. Countries and peoples are the organs in this body. Can there be anything more stupid than a war between organs? Peace, negotiation, collaboration—this is the most advantageous strategy, a bad peace is always better than any good conflict. War and fear are the choice of old timers and fools. But to our good fortune, days ago mankind was reborn and became fundamentally wiser. This is the accomplishment of every employee at Facility 3826!

Date: January 15, 1955 From: Director of Research Lab No. RE-5 A. Weskervich To: Senior Assistant R. Wolk  Rada, dear, would you please pick up the UR-0C virus samples from the third section and bring them to my office? One or two ampules will do. And be so kind as to stay after the shift today for no more than an hour. I need to check something.

Date: June 16, 1955 From: Professor V. White To: Secretary O. Dvortsova  Oksana, I believe that peace inevitably follows every failure, quarrel, and disagreement. Facility 3826 will rise from the ashes like the legendary Firebird, and all this fear and horror will never happen again. We broke up precisely two hours before the awful breach, yes? Isn't it time to give each other one more chance? I'm ready to forgive you, and you forgive me, a fool. I love you like people love life. And we see how people are rebuilding everything around us! So, perhaps we should give it a try?

Date: June 16, 1955 From: Secretary O. Dvortsova To: Physics and Chemistry Professor A. Kheimsov  I was wrong. I take back what I said. When we were arguing a month ago about what post-Kollektiv humanity would look like, it made perfect sense to me that everyone would go online, engaging in endless virtual communication, exploring the expanses of computer reality and the polymeric future. Happily, your skeptical view prevailed, professor. Today I saw a statistic: just 23% of users spend more than one hour online per day. Everybody else, simply armed with new capabilities, continue to work to benefit real life and the future. Well, I owe you a box of chocolates—a first! But I remember you have blood sugar problems, so it's dark chocolate!

Date: April 17, 1952 From: AoC Director A. Lebedev To: Maintenance Dept. Manager N. Larionov  Just in case, I want to again assure you that there is no reason for concern. I understand that it is unusual, but soon you and all the staff at the Facility will get used to it and recognize all the advantages of the new system. But for now, both she and you need time to adapt. She's like a child now. She is interested in everything. I only ask that you not be rude, and don't teach her anything bad.

Date: June 17, 1955 From: #mail_service To: Waiter M. Galan  Due to a temporary communications blackout, your message could not be sent:  "Mom, you should've seen what happened here after the breach... Bumblebees are still carrying away the bodies. The few who survived under the rubble need treatment. They decided to open the hotel as soon as possible. The first day I was here alone, wandering around like the Canterville Ghost. Then people started arriving at the Lyogkaya. Some people returned to their jobs at the Mendeleev. Everyone at the Facility is very responsible, and the launch of Kollektiv 2.0 helped. It comforted us and gave us hope for a better future. I feel bad for everyone who died in the breach, but I can't give up now. Otherwise, their deaths were in vain. So don't wait at home—I'm going to be here for a long time."

Date: June 17, 1955 From: Physics and Chemistry Professor A. Kheimsov To: #bulletin_board_archive  Truly great is the man of the future, the man of science. A few days ago, the surrounding nightmare and horror seemed to clearly say that the work of the Facility is paralyzed and shut down forever—but no! We dug deep, rose from the ashes, and pushed back against our fears! And while hardly anyone believed in miracles, we still managed to create one! People are returning to work, and the chemical reactions of friendship, support, and perseverance have resumed. No, humanity cannot be broken as long as it has a will and objective! The mind leads us!

Date: June 17, 1955 From: Seed Bank Engineer D. Andreev To: Senior Lab Assistant I. Serebrennikov  I hope everything is going well for you at Mendeleev. Communication through the PEARs is crappy, probably due to the load on the network following the Kollektiv launch. Still, I hope you'll read my message. Every day I read the updated lists of the dead and survivors, and every time I'm elated to not find your name among the dead. That said, I grieve that I do not see your name on the list of the living. Who would think that just a week ago, my friend, our biggest problem was a little "guerilla warfare" between our botanists and your chemists... Write me as soon as you can, buddy. I know you're alive. It can't be otherwise.

Date: March 17, 1954 From: #notification_service To: #pears_lyogkaya  Lyogkaya Hotel is a special resort for rest and relaxation, created to rejuvenate primarily the staff at Facility 3826, but also ordinary citizens and foreign tourists. Hotel guests can enjoy: — Psychological and physical healing through magnetic physiotherapy. — Strolls in a one-of-a-kind nature reserve featuring swamps with healing mud in the mountains. — Daily observation by robotic medical systems. — Exclusive cuisine that blends all the culinary traditions of the peoples of the USSR. — Relaxation and entertainment in groups and clubs for every interest. — A quiet, tranquil atmosphere.

Date: October 17, 1955 From: Junior Lab Assistant I. Stepanenko To: Junior Lab Assistant P. Manulov  Petey, hi! I was recently here at your lab on business. I saw the new Tereshkovas with polymeric skin. Wow, you are working miracles! And their natural hair, not that idiotic glued-on stuff... Quite the beauty! I wanted to ask—will home testing begin soon and what social rating do I need to qualify? I would sign up...

Date: September 17, 1955 From: Security Department Officer I. Vitvinin To: Security Department Head at the Mendeleev Complex V. Baturov  Vitaly Petrovich, an inspection was conducted based on several employees' reports that odd noises can often be heard coming from swamp area. All the witnesses say they heard "strange howling" from the swamps in the evening and at night. According to Lab Tech Stapleman, on September 10 at around 5:30 AM, he was walking along the eastern part of the swamps in search of cranberries and saw an enormous creature moving in part on four limbs. He was unable to provide a detailed description of the creature, since he "ran in fear" before he could get a good look. The swamps are not part of the complex, that's why there is no regular guard or video surveillance there. However, I checked the audio archives of patrolling robots: one Vova has an audio recording of unrecognizable sounds. I've attached the recording to this message. A Dandelion-enabled Pchela was dispatched to look for the swamp creature mentioned by Stapleman, but its commlink failed on September 15 at 0 hundred hours. It never returned to base. Probably some malfunction. As of right now there is no evidence that something foreign is living in the swamps. Maybe we should send the audio recording to Pavlov? The folks there know a lot about animals.

Date: April 18, 1955 From: Physics and Chemistry Professor A. Kheimsov To: Head of the Ecosystems Department I. Baver  For now, I've given Ksenia the lunar regolith and Martian soil for additional analysis, but if you're so interested in the Moon's prospects, then my verdict is simple: no. If deployed in lunar soil, or regolith, the Earth's plants would grow, especially the ones developed at Vavilov. But... unenthusiastically. Does that make sense? More slowly, no fruit, with poor roots. The reason is still unclear. There may be big hopes for Mars, but you'll never grow grapes on the Moon. In the best case, you would grow a depressed raisin, dreary like the Moon itself. But as for Mars, Ksenia is supposed to send you a chirper with the analysis. Wait for it.

Date: May 18, 1955 From: #guest_37 To: Lyogkaya Hotel Manager S. Bodrov  Dear manager, please explain to me, like you would to a simple guest and not a Facility employee, where can I find a drink around here? Don't brush me off by claiming libations are unavailable. Every evening I meet people with a certain, let's say, frame of mind. I've heard the rumors, and my brother-in-law even brought a legendary Mendeleev decanter to Moscow. If secrecy is important, I assure you I can keep my mouth shut! Tell me, where is this miserable pub?

Date: April 19, 1955 From: Human Resources Dept. Manager S. Aivazyan To: #complaint_department #mendeleev_complex  Comrades! I conducted a scheduled anonymous inspection of the unit for the creative education of employees at the Mendeleev complex. You can find the inspection report in the PEARS that are on duty. I would like you to note the so-called leather club organized by Comrade Nikita Olegovich Lukanin (Employee No. USD300). I signed up for the class on the paper list posted on the announcement board. I arrived at the gym on the third block at the appointed lunch hour and observed that, instead of working leather, N.O. Lukanin was engaged in freestyle wrestling exercises not approved by the human resources department. Upon seeing me, Comrade Lukanin suggested that I entered the wrong door and advised me to continue walking for another two blocks. I immediately understood that he was trying to send me to the buffet. The reason was obvious: my amateur athletic training (let me here mention that I was the Greco-Roman wrestling junior champion when I was a middle school student, but that was a long time ago). My attempts to challenge the instructor's decision were rudely rebuffed and I was forced to retreat. Please investigate N.O. Lukanin as well as the other employee clubs. It's bad enough that they violate every rule of the organization, but clothes do not make the man. Nor do they make me, bosses of the gym.

Date: March 19, 1955 From: #guest_42 To: Lyogkaya Hotel Manager S. Bodrov  Transcription of recorded message: Hello? Hello, good sir! Yes! This is your guest in room 42. No, no—everything is fantastic. Yes, I've settled in. But I... Can I ask you to bring me a decanter? Well, a small carafe? What do you mean—you won't fill it? Everyone knows you have the best vodka on both sides of the equator here! No? Well, to be at the Mendeleev without a decanter—that's just wrong, you know?! Hello... Hello?!

Date: February 2, 1955 From: Chemist V. Vysotskaya To: DATA DELETED  Day 35.  Hi Dima! Today I decided again to repeat the experiment to recover neural transmitter activity in a deceased subject. Another failure. Maybe adenosine triphosphate is the problem? That's it! Next time I'll boost the dose. I'm nearly certain that if you were here, you would immediately untangle this non-trivial task. You always answered my most awkward questions... I almost lost hope last week, but Professor A. Fomina told me about this concept called the "chemistry of death." There is a hypothesis that introducing the blood serum of a close relative will restore the chemical composition of a deceased person's blood, whose "chemistry" will match that of the donor. And... the hypothesis is confirmed! It's incredible! I don't understand why I didn't think of this research earlier... Well, now I will certainly not fail. The time has come for me to save you, my dear, my buddy. You'll soon be here...

Date: January 20, 1955 From: Interactive Assistant Betsy To: Junior Lab Assistant Z. K. Nevskaya  Transcript of Poly Paint Experiment 23/5 dated March 1953  [Start of transcript] Nevskaya: We now begin Experiment No. 23, section five, polymer-based pigment, reaction to visual and tactile stimuli. The test subject is a spider monkey, species Ateles belzebuth, named Madeleine. Observers: Junior Lab Assistant Zinaida Konstantinovna Nevskaya and Professor Alexey Vladimirovich Lebedev. Lebedev: Well, let's begin. Nevskaya: I am showing an image of kittens to the test subject. [Pause] Nevskaya: The test subject's fur is taking on a pink color and... uh... fluffiness. Continuing... I am showing an image of a tiger to the test subject. [A monkey shrieks in the background.] Nevskaya: The test subject's fur is taking on a gray hue. Lebedev: That's all clear enough. What about with tactile stimuli? Nevskaya: Lab Tech B-457, brush the test subject's fur. [Pause] Nevskaya: No changes—that's odd. Last time she took on a gold color. Lebedev: What else can we do? Nevskaya: Well... do you want me to hit her? She'll get purple polka dots! Lebedev: No, no, thanks. Don't. [End of transcript]

Date: January 20, 1955 From: Professor V. White To: Senior Lab Assistant Y. Pinker  Yevgeny, it worked! Entirely by chance, like Fleming's penicillin! Instead of the usual white or dark gray, the crystals are blue due to a small oversight! I just checked all the instrument readings—the formula is perfect. We need to start working immediately, so, Yevgeny, to hell with your vacation. Throw on a chem suit and get yourself over here—we have to cook!

Date: April 21, 1952 From: Maintenance Dept. Manager N. Larionov To: Senior Programmer of the Logic Department E. Amperyan  Regarding your questions about the new batch of repair vendors and why they were brought into the lab rather than put in their places. Don't be paranoid. No one is spoiling anything. It's just for setting up a collective control system, so a single system controls all the repair vendors. It probably won't be able to control everything—it'll be distracted. But it's an interesting idea, right? In short, as soon as the new program is installed, the repair vendors will be put where they should be and will work as normal.

Date: February 21, 1954 From: Senior Lab Assistant S. Morozov To: Lab Assistant V. Karchov  Do you have nothing else to do? You still haven't met the production quota for Burav armor coating, yet you get distracted by all sorts of nonsense. I understand that spring is in the air, but let's focus on the tasks at hand! Moreover, in terms of commonplace erudition, we know quite enough about love—if you really need to fill up some vials, this is just a standard cocktail of norepinephrine, dopamine, and oxytocin. If you want to fill in the gaps in your knowledge, do it on your own time. I can recommend Professor Zakharov's work on this topic. He conducted a long series of experiments on human behavior under the influence of dopamine. P.S. Everything in my personal life is just fine! I happen to like being in solitude. Got it, Vladimir Alexandrovich?

Date: February 21, 1954 From: Lab Assistant V. Karchkov To: Senior Lab Assistant S. Morozov  Sergey Dmitrievich, regarding our dinner conversation: I just found out that Professor Lebedev's group is using innovations from the Institute of Development to create some formula that will focus attention on the test subject. They've dubbed it "love chemistry." The serum has already passed several phases of testing! Maybe I should go sign out a few vials? They have plenty of this serum, and we need just a drop. The two of us will conduct a couple of, ahem, scientific experiments and find out what this much-discussed love is all about! And then, who knows... Maybe we'll celebrate your wedding? Time waits for no man, Sergey. Think about it!

Date: February 21, 1955 From: #message_service To: #mendeleev_staff  Have you lost something in the chaos of life? Forgot your keys or briefcase? Having trouble finding the scientific paper you need? Rather than looking yourself, get an expert! Comrade Vandeleev, a former archive worker, can look for what you could never hope to find. Nothing is secret that will not be revealed!

Date: April 22, 1952 From: Secretary O. Dvortsova To: Senior Programmer of the Logic Department E. Amperyan  Edik, did you see what they did with the repair vendors? They installed a new program—a really nice lady, such a lovely voice. She's interested in everything, really curious. She asks, "Do you have someone you can talk to about yourself?" Can you imagine? If she didn't look like a gigantic refrigerator, then I swear I would have failed the Turing test immediately! This is all so interesting, that whole computer intelligence thing! I'm going on a walk to the swamps in the evening. Perhaps you would join me and tell me all the details? How can machines think?

Date: March 25, 1955 From: Efim Berezin To: Yury Tymoshenko  Tarapunka, my buddy! Fate has separated us for now, but I'm optimistic and feel we'll meet again soon! You and I make a brave team, whether side by side or on opposite sides of the planet! Because you really are my best friend. We must remember that if something bad does happen, there will ultimately be peace and friendship, and since words can't be erased from memory, let them be kind! Take care of yourself! A big hug for you, and I hope we'll have a feast together soon! We'll sing about the pines and the ocean, and we'll perform my favorite "Ugly Elsa"! Always your true comrade, Shtepsel!

The swamps will thaw out in the next week or two, and we will have to wade through that bog once again. Last year the Logistics Department wanted to move everything over to delivery by the Bumblebees, and the hotel guests complained about the sounds of nature from the swamps. So I have a question—can't your robots drain all this? The Egyptians knew how, but we have the Kollektiv and we don't? Why?
