Soviet radio performer Vera Vershinina's incredible, poignant voice became legendary throughout the Soviet Union when she was chosen to become the voice of the Deimos OS virtual assistant in June 1950. Comrade Vershinina's personality and vocal tone was so well-liked at the Chelomey Design Bureau that she quickly become the official voice of Facility 3826. If you talk to a computer, it will answer you in Comrade Vershinina's voice.

Burak was recently appointed to the post of exhibit curator by the Ministry of Culture. Despite his magnificent recommendations and excellent work history, he has struggled to fit in at the strict, buttoned-down VDNH. The HR department receives complaints about his rudeness, excessive familiarity, and condescending attitude toward employees on a nearly weekly basis. However, upper management has been extremely positive about the new hire, noting his fresh perspective on how exhibit pieces are presented and implemented. "Comrade Burak has such an innovative view of things that impetuous new behaviors are always just a step away," said a complaint against Comrade Burak filed on behalf of the VDNH Tour Guide Union.

A German scientist of Jewish descent, Stockhausen worked as a doctor in Berlin during the war. He lived through the first outbreaks of the Brown Plague and was later saved by Soviet soldiers. Prior to his infection, he had an incredible memory—a fact his coworkers could attest to—but lost this ability after the onset of the illness and never demonstrated it again (although he does not regret the loss).  Thanks to his scientific and organizational talents, Stockhausen's career enjoyed a startlingly rapid ascent. He was recruited to the Facility in order to fill a quota for scientists from the German Soviet Socialist Republic and quickly earned Sechenov's respect. Despite his German pedantry and a certain degree of snobbishness, he remains one of the best-known—and best-liked—members of the Facility 3826 team. He is perfectly capable of speaking Russian without an accent, but chooses to "sound German" in order to remind people of his origins.

Sherman was sent to Vavilov in order to fill a quota for specialists from the German Soviet Socialist Republic. Her primary specialization isn't plants or genes, but rather designing essential equipment and reviewing requests from specialists in various fields.

Few people have met the director of the AoC, who is also a leading Soviet programmer and the creator of the Aldan supercomputer. Most employees don't even know that this man exists, but he has actually replaced Comrade Lebedev as the head of the Academy of Consequences' top-secret Neptune facility.

Although his last name is derived from the Russian word for "caramel," Karamelkin is anything but sweet. Everyone knows that he is excessively rude to rule-breakers and can even get physical with more serious violators. Despite this, there is no denying that the theft of drugs and equipment has been reduced fourfold since he assumed his current position. Comrade Karamelkin is fully cognizant of his place at the Facility and in the world at large. Some aspects of his personality suggest a high degree of discipline, while others are nothing more than bad habits. "Everything's fine," Karamelkin mutters before returning to his usual duties.

Comrade Lastochkin is not a traditional theater director. Better known as "Stefan," Lastochkin has had a stunning career, starting out as an office manager and becoming the head of what is perhaps the most famous theater in the world. In less than a year, unique performances such as "The Binding Screws of Friendship," "In the Vice of Passion," and the modern classic "Electric Origins" have become sensations among fans of avant-garde art. However, his narcissism, shady dealings, and despotic management style have set many theater employees at odds with the ambitious new director.

The theater's new office manager, Surkov is an elderly, experienced man who has worked at the Bolshoi and overseen performances on the front lines for soldiers. An honest, but also one-dimensional and somewhat cantankerous old man, Surkov often has harsh words for management and anyone else who draws his ire.

A recent hire, Vishnevskaya was brought on to replace a senior programmer who was fired for inappropriate conduct. She is known as a suffragette, social activist, and active proponent of women's rights. Vishnevskaya is beloved by her coworkers for her responsibility and friendliness.

Elena Krayeva is an exemplary Soviet citizen. Carefree and outgoing, she has long been a regular sight at Pavlov Complex cultural events. Along with her pleasant, friendly personality, Comrade Krayeva is also known for her great passion for her work and has been recognized as a hero of communist labor three years in a row.

One of the leading dog trainers in the Soviet Union, or "Pavlov's Dog," as he jokingly calls himself, Gromyko is a crucial member of the Facility 3826 staff. His published works on raising, training, and cross-breeding species have been translated into 64 languages, five of them by himself. However, despite all his talents and service to the Motherland, this modest dog breeder prefers the company of his four-legged friends to scientific debates. Especially valuable in light of Polymer-based biotechnology is his work on breeding and training martian and lunar "dogs," i.e. the Polymer-based organisms known as Plyusch, which, thanks to Comrade Gromyko's hard work and care, are now exemplary, obedient representatives of man's future interplanetary best friend.

One of the highest-ranking leaders in the Communist Party, Molotov is also the President of the Council of Ministers and a political opponent of Comrade Sechenov. A talented politician used to operate on an international scale, he was made the overseer of Facility 3826 by the CPSU Central Committee and the Council of Ministers.

One of the Facility's managers, Yelizarova is in charge of the VDNH's exhibits and visitor interaction. She stood out from the very beginning of her tenure at the Facility and is responsible for the creation of the VDNH. Rumor has it she had to personally convince Dr. Sechenov of the need for a museum, and her efforts have clearly been vindicated.

Oleg: Holy moly, I thought the robot breach only happened to us at Triton. So much for getting to safety.  Vyacheslav: Still better to be on dry land than marinating on the lake bottom. It's just a shame we don't have guns or a ploughing fence board.  Oleg: And what will you do? Throw yourself against the embrasure like Matrosov? We're not really the robot-fighting type, Vyacheslav Batkovich.  RAF-9: Human presence detected. Comrades, please prepare for liquidation. Thank you.  Oleg: Patrol!  Vyacheslav: Red Pchela! Thirty seconds until we're royally fucked! Quiet, looks like it hasn't seen us...  RAF-9: Ready or not, here I come!  Oleg: You won't take us!  Vyacheslav: Oleg, no!  Stranger: Move! You're not dying today!  RAF-9: Damage! Damage! Analyzing...  Stranger: Analyze this, bitch!  Stranger: What the hell were you thinking, huh? You get sick of breathing, man?  Oleg: W-well, I just... entered combat mode in the end...  Stranger: Uh... Life's hard, but it has to be done. Your buddy too. Just put the broomstick down. It's over.  Vyacheslav: We just took what we had on hand.  Stranger: Commendable. I need to get to the Triton complex. Come with me if you want to live.  Oleg: Sorry, but I doubt...  Vyacheslav: Who are you?  Stranger: Me? I'm the Hunter.

An experienced specialist in her department, Meglina has become quite well-known in certain circles thanks to her analytical mind. The valedictorian at her university, she has a gift for studying available materials and drawing exceedingly refined, elegant conclusions from them. Just give Yevgenia Meglina a few data points, and she'll spit out an analysis before you can blink.

An experienced specialist, Nazarov is one of the creators of Polymer-based express printing technology, which has increased the speed of the Facility's printing dozens of times over. He runs the VDNH's printing department, but is actually responsible for all printed material throughout the Facility.

Yefremov admits that he dreamed of becoming an actor as a child, but, after working in security, he has dedicated his life to the theater in another capacity. His magnificent record as a Facility 3826 roboticist began with repairing robotic ballerinas at the Plisetskaya Theater, but he was soon promoted to a more senior position at the VDNH. His coworkers consider him an extremely friendly, fun-loving, and inventive expert with a natural sense of flair.

It may sound macabre, but for morgue supervisor Gireyev, dead people are the love of his life. Having begun his career as a gravedigger at a Moscow cemetery in imperial Russia before the revolution, Gireyev's career has involved exhuming bodies, destroying the corpses of people killed by the Brown Plague, and overseeing funerals for unknown soldiers after the war. He rarely makes jokes, but is "more comfortable with the dead, since no one's ever had his life ruined by a corpse."
President of the Council of Ministers

Nicknamed "Koschevna" after Koschey, a character from Russian folklore whose soul is hidden within a series of nested items, Khodyukova matches her facetious moniker to a tee. Not even an entire team of Complex and project managers could vie with her when it comes to accounting skills. She is particularly concerned with her social rating, but always endeavors to work efficiently enough to top the chart. Accounts payable, expense reports, endless contracts—she mentally catalogs all this information with such perfection that Professor Zakharov once joked that Kollektiv's system should not be built on Neuropolymers, but planned by Nonna Khodyukova.

Nyukhov was a special operative and intelligence officer during the war. After WWII he served as a supply officer, actively fighting against "enemies of the people" and the Brown Plague. He personally arrested Comrade Vavilov on Stalin's order, but later became the botanist's close friend and comrade despite this. Nyukhov was assigned to his current position immediately after the complex was created.

Radio transmission: ...Dr. Sechenov just held a press conference in which he completely denied rumors about civilian robots malfunctioning at Facility 3826. The Facility is back to full operational capacity, and the red alert will be lifted very soon. Kollektiv 2.0 will be launched as planned.  Rescuer: There! Get it now?! I repeat for the last time, comrade... the breach has been fixed! Now, hand over your rifle.  Hunter: No, thanks. I didn't crawl here on my belly, shooting robots the whole way, just to hand over my gun to some snot-nosed kid. You'll thank me later when it happens all over again!  Rescuer: Thanks, but no thanks. Listen, you've had to go through a lot, I understand. But please enough with the paranoia and panic, comrade! Go home and get some rest. Life moves pretty fast, so stop and look around once in a while. Or just enjoy the launch of Kollektiv 2.0.  Hunter: Life?! You know, in the war, they shot panic-mongers first for demoralization. That's the truth. Too early to count your losses.  Rescuer: One more word, Comrade... whatever your name is... and I'll detain you!  Hunter: I didn't introduce myself. Hit the ground, lieutenant, quick!  Rescuer: Fuck! Control, this is Windmill-2. The robots resumed their attack. I repeat: robots in combat mode!  Hunter: I was right, and you weren't. Take my hand, let's find cover. All's about to be blown to kingdom come!

Radio operator: Comrade Afanasiev, I hasten to inform you that I heard the quacking again tonight...  Lab director: You again, Comrade Operator.  Radio operator: And not just one tone! At least three! I assure you, I am not making this up. I heard it with my own ears! And it's not just underwater vibration. It's something... alive...  Passerby: Hello, Comrade Lab Director.  Radio operator: I even... Good evening.  Lab director: Hello.  Radio operator: I even have a detailed report. I recorded everything! I know you don't want to talk to me, but I implore you: just listen to it yourself. You'll hear it. You just have to take a close look into the abyss and... listen.

Radon: You think the Major is a traitor? What's he doing here?  Krypton: Traitor? Come on. He's a loyal dog, and he's been on medication for a few years. But... That's not for us to handle. Let's pick him up.  Radon: Well, yeah... But the fact that he survived against both Twins... I'm glad he's alive. It's just unexpected.  Krypton: All's unexpected here. Lean him there, yeah. Careful! Our orders are not to harm the bodies.  Radon: But who gave the order? Wizard hasn't been in contact, and Argon disappeared.  Krypton: Take him! The order came over a secret line under Sechenov's cipher. Put him here. Our job is to carry out the orders, not discuss them. Lay him here. We'll take them both with us once we reclaim Chelomey.  Radon: I wonder if this is Right or Left?  Krypton: Who can ever tell? The one with a jacket is Left. Or Right. It's good we found at least one.  Radon: Damn. Well, Plutonium's really heavy...  Krypton: No wonder. He's stuffed with PTA-6... And he's P-3 now and not Plutonium anymore. Hmm, wait. Why the hell is your chirper on...?  Radon: I didn't... Fuck, they're listening!  Krypton: Robots! Take cover!

Alexey Lebedev is an electrical engineer and energy specialist and the founder of Soviet computing technology. He was the head of the All-Russian Electronics Institute's automation department and the director of the Institute of Precision Mechanics and Computing Technology. Lebedev created the first electronic analog computing machine in the country in order to solve ordinary differential equations that are frequently encountered in energy-related fields. The first small electronic calculation machine in the Soviet Union and Continental Europe was also developed under his leadership. He is the head of a top-secret AoC department, but, thanks to his friend and colleague Privalov, he has been able to free himself from administrative duties and continue studying the quantum entanglement of radio waves. The Radio of the Future is his most cherished and inimitable creation.

Confident, sarcastic, talented—all these qualities commingle in Dr. Grigory Domov. A unique specialist, he has become a real Pavlov Complex legend thanks to his almost superhuman ability to correctly diagnose 99% of cases. However, flawlessly performing his duties is not the only thing Comrade Domov is known for at the hospital. His coworkers know him first and foremost for his love of pranks, which sometimes go beyond the bounds of common sense. But Comrade Domov is not the least bit troubled by his sense of humor. Knowing full well that he is ultimately irreplaceable, Domov often finds ways to overshadow his stunning accomplishments by flagrantly violating the chain of command.

Samokhin: Dima, have you ever read Moby Dick? As a whale biologist.  Tikhonov: No, but I know the gist... Wait. Are you comparing me to a whaler? Really? By the way, did you know our complex has tripled the population of gray whales in two years? And if a couple had to be taken apart in the process, then—  Samokhin: Wait. I just finished it, and I can't figure out how it could be possible to annihilate creatures with high intelligence and a complicated communication system. Sentient beings!  Tikhonov: You know what, my impressionable friend? Read your Scholastic Magazines, stop distracting me from work.

Svetlana: Hi, Dante. How are you feeling today? Any improvements?  Dante the dolphin: No. But thanks for asking, Lab Tech Svetlana. I think I've found the answer to my philosophical question, though.  Svetlana: Which one? Want a fish?  Dante the dolphin: Yes, thank you. I've become interested in why we dolphins... change so much working with you.  Svetlana: Well, that seems quite obvious to me. We communicate, learn from each other, exchange skills...  Dante the dolphin: Exactly! We learn from you. Your language, communication habits, even swearing. And, as a result, your way of thinking. But this is a one-sided game, as Nale likes to say.  Svetlana: Can you elaborate?  Dante the dolphin: We don't learn from each other. Dolphins only learn from humans. And just like the robots, you make everything look like you. Forgive my frankness, but you revel in anthropomorphism, and... contaminate us, and everything else with... humanity.  Svetlana: Wow, point-blank! But perhaps you're right. Thanks, Dante. By the way, do you know what pareidolia is? It's when humans start seeing living things in inanimate objects.  Dante the dolphin: Pareidolia is a visual illusion, Svetlana. I'm talking about something else! Anyway, it's fine. Can I at least have some more fish?

Secretary: Colleagues, we have a code red. A scandal threatens, and that's right before polymerization! The famous chess player David Bronstein came to visit. So, they decided to show him Nastya Nazarova's dolphin chess club. And Comrade Grandmaster, as part of entertainment program, decided he'd like to play chess with a dolphin. And... Ooh, I'm gonna burst... Ha ha! Well, he won, our dolphin won! He didn't crush him immediately, of course, but... something still got crushed! Heh!  In short, leadership requests that we sweep this under the rug so it doesn't get out before Kollektiv 2.0 launches. They might say they won't give commands to robots, but serve dolphins instead. Hilarious, naturally!  Look into it, or else everyone will know what a disgrace to the Soviet school of chess we are!

Semyon: Don't go yet, Lida! I wanted to read you something...  Lida: Why are you blushing, Semyon?  Semyon: I met a traveler from an antique land Who said: Two vast and trunkless legs of stone Stand in the desert. Near them, on the sand, Half sunk, a shattered visage lies, whose frown, And wrinkled lip, and sneer of cold command, Tell that its sculptor well those passions read Which yet survive, stamped on these lifeless things, The hand that mocked them and the heart that fed:  And on the pedestal, these words appear: "My name is Ozymandias, king of kings; Look on my works, ye Mighty, and despair!"  Nothing beside remains. Round the decay Of that colossal wreck, boundless and bare The lone and level sands stretch far away.  Lida: What a striking poem!  Semyon: Percy Bysshe Shelley, 1817.  Lida: But what do you think it's about, Semyon?  Semyon: How nothing lasts forever. And it's terrifying to look into the future because it's utterly unknowable.  Lida: You're a philosopher, Semyon. But don't be so glum. I'm sure our future's bright.  Semyon: May I join you? You're going to the town square to listen to Dr. Sechenov's speech, right?  Lida: Sure, let's go.

Security employee: Nikolai Semyonovich, this is shore patrol. I noticed odd figures on the shore last night. Not people, but they didn't look like robots, either. I think they were burying something. That area's restricted. I sent a warning shot up in the air, and they jumped in the water. We've posted guards, so nothing like that will slip past again. If these are your experimental freaks from the underwater Research Center, come and get them. Or it'll be like the dolphin incident. That was awkward. How is he, by the way? Recovered? I haven't written my report yet. Been on leave since Friday, so... Well, for old times' sake. Bye.
An expert writer of scientific papers, Malakhova is also the genetic engineering department's press secretary, overseeing scientific reports and acting as an editor and censor.

Reufe is an expert on prisoner psychology and criminal behavior. Every prisoner sentenced to community service has talked to him. Scrupulous and careful, he is known as a cold, thoughtful, and reclusive individual.

Senior technician: We've accepted this package, Vadim. We sent it down to the Research Center and allocated a room in Triton. What's going on there is pretty scary—people dead all around, everything busted to hell, and these soulless creatures just stand there without a command. Can you imagine? It almost made me cry. One of those lab tech robots was just leaning against the wall as if ashamed, and his face was just... blank! Totally blank! Who's responsible for this now?  Speaking of a responsible person... What's with the damned Muscovite they sent here with the package? He's got no documents, not even our chevrons. What's with that? Is he even from the Facility?

Terentiy: Oh, comrades! It's a chirper! How fortunate! Come in, come in! He's got a mitten! Terentiy here! People don't understand even simple algorithms. Where am I going with this? Ever since Comrade Lebedev sent me to Zinaida, she has given me a lot of hard work. Robots don't understand what work is, so I'm not upset. I'm probably just a romantic. I've run away from Grandpa, from robots, from evildoers, but not from Granny. I'll open a robot bar. Terentiy's. That sounds good. I must be going. I cannot stay. I came to say, "I must be going." It seems I need to return to work, comrades. Bye!

Technically speaking, Orlikova is the Academy of Consequences' representative at Vavilov Complex. She collects archival materials, sets security levels, and maintains communication between the Academy and the Complex. Despite the importance of her position, she has a good sense of humor and is easygoing with coworkers. However, there is no one living who could extract even the most inconsequential secret about Facility 3826 from Maria Orlikova.

Comrade Verestenyets is truly a unique citizen—as the manager of the Maya Plisetskaya Theater cafeteria, she not only knows all its baking-related equipment inside and out, but also remembers the names of every ballet pose ever performed on the theater's stage. She has her repertoire for the next year committed to memory and can tell you which seat and row are best for viewing a given performance. Few people know that this remarkable woman has a PhD, but absolutely everyone she works with knows about her love for the arts. For Comrade Verestenyets, ballet is her greatest, most cherished dream.

Comrade Lebedyansky is an engineer and train builder. He was involved in the design and construction of the largest Soviet locomotives and armored trains, including the Felix Dzerzhinsky, the Joseph Stalin, and the Victory. After the war, he switched to designing cutting-edge diesel and gas turbine locomotives that attained record speeds and replaced ordinary trains on Soviet railways.  The inventor is currently involved in testing magnetic levitation or Maglev railways at Facility 3826. Vortex automatic trains will soon crisscross the entire country, extending to even the most distant reaches of the Soviet Union.

A demanding, pushy woman, Debaltovskaya has earned a reputation as a headstrong person that even upper management would be reluctant to quarrel with. She is a born manager. Academy employees work under her supervision day and night, and their productivity has significantly improved since Debaltovskaya took over the position.

Who knows, honey? You're a military man, so you understand it's not weapons that kill people...
How do I disable the ORB?
How did you manage to get me?
As you wish, darling. But keep in mind that I have information about your wife. It won't be saved after recombination!
What's the difference? It's her own choice! Surely, you weren't talking about me just now, were you, darling?
What experiment? Is the device working? I don't understand, have you managed to get in Limbo or not? Have you found your v... what an idiot I am!
My little grumpy cat! Okay, go on and think.
You're so generous! I belong to you alone! We're a perfect match, darling!
Shit, the rings! The beta connectors! The whole unit was hunting them down, and Charles persuaded me to throw them away. He said they'd only cause trouble!
Avalanche-1 calling Red-3, come in, Red-3. Do a barrel roll!
Who said that? That nasty hag? Or the boring old man? Don't believe a single word!
Chemistry research can be found anywhere, except in one place: time! Time is the only place chemical processes do not occur!
Puppets?! Okay, whatever. I'm gonna go talk to her. You stay here and don't go anywhere.
Okay, that's it, that's the last fucking Alionka. That's the last Alionka. I wish I had a hundred kilos on hand! Mmm! I wish I could count calories! How am I supposed to count calories?
Fine. Tell me what you know.
Okay, I'll wait until the common beads join up around the carrier.
I'd thank you if you took it out, but you're just another manipulator. Crispy... I'm so sick of you all!
If only I could be a proud single woman and never mess with a man!
I brought you to our cozy family nest, sugar! The entire complex is ours now!
Darling, please, I'm begging you! Don't deprive me of my individuality. I want to be able to choose how I live my life! This isn't fair!
How was your walk, darling? That vicious old hag is jamming my signal to the surface! Were you able to negotiate with her?
You don't want to fly away from me in this Komar, do you, honey? I erased the launch code just in case! We'll be together forever! Aren't you happy?
The little rascals are too independent. They choose their own configuration! Are you sure you won't change your mind about giving me this little beady, honey?
I'm only interested in you, my darling! Other people are boring and primitive.
Darling! That slut Filatova just pulled the tracking sensor out of the brain of that unworthy slug!
Sugar, you leave me no choice! Personal freedom is more precious than your false love.
I like your attitude, darling. I want more!
Don't I know it. See you.
I could have! But I was so interested in seeing your famous wit come out, my darling!
Mighty leopard, you always land on your strong feet! Does it hurt?
Maybe the Kollektiv was created for the benefit of people, but clearly not those who died here by the hundred. And society doesn't care!
Maybe you were fighting with some memory, maybe just with that witch in your head.
Can I say that curse word now?
We're a team, sweetheart! It turns out that helping you is so much fun!
You'll find the neuropolymeric launch module, on the table by the exit. Activate it when things get really difficult, and I'll come to help you!
As far as I know, the Facility doesn't emphasize one science over another. They're all interconnected.
I won't. They're way off the mark. You're not crazy, just eccentric.
You don't believe me, comrade. You're mocking me.
It won't work, honey! This sector generates the electromagnetic trap that keeps the nasty old hag from hurting me and the boring old man from flying out!
You'll do it, darling! You are so brave! Crafty! Skillful!
Don't even think about it, sugar. You're not going to impose your will on me! A woman has the right to decide how she wants to live her life!
Don't give me dunno! You've got a brain the size of a planet!
I can't, darling! It's... part of a defense protocol. It activates automatically and stuff...
That's not true! There have been moments of silence all around the cities! They showed them on TV!
Take your time, darling! We need one of those!
That doesn't matter. I need to talk to Lebedev.
Not much, surprisingly. I've been slinging drinks here a long time. Folks often said she was once some kind of psychologist.
Not many, but all of them. After the Kollektiv breach, not everyone decided to go back to work. Some died then, you've been there.
No glove, no protection, remember? Ha! You did everything right, darling!
The scanner won't work without CHAR-les.
No, but I can sense when it's around.
There will never be anyone here! No one to ever disturb our happiness together!
No one can outrun death, no one can stop it. So you can just take it out of the equation and live happily ever after.
Nothing sets you up right for work like good collective effort!
But you're right—it would be a nightmare to die like that on your first day of work!
But the system didn't last long. People were either panicked or afraid, and communicating with her was deeply embarrassing to some, so the project was scrapped.
But they tried to rehabilitate the ones that survived. The hotel was full.
A normal life. And the truth.
But carriers are painted in special colors.
And? Why should I care about others? Why should I have to obey someone else when I have my own free will?!
Dopamine capsules. Was it not enough? Like I said, I can't get you anymore. But hey, the Kollektiv launched. Check the network for where to get them.
But of course, sweety, that's how it went! Like I said, I trust you completely.
Don't be mad. I'll let you out for a walk, my playful puppy!
Well, I can't go any further, and I doubt I can drive that old hag away. Can't you do something?
Well, I'm young. Emotions, you know? Chemistry is in my blood! My whole life is ahead of me!
Well, that's good, at least! You couldn't have warned me about that either, huh?
That's not up to you, young man.
Well, "resting in peace" does include "resting." There's no point in being sad when resting, eh? Especially with a clear mind!
Oh yes! Explain to her that she's wasting her time, darling. Let her leave so we can enjoy our happy family!
Oh, there are beautiful places to walk up top. But you have to come back as soon as you talk to the old hag!
I can't, master! There's a padlock on the inside! It's a huge warehouse one. But you can get out through the door upstairs—that one's not locked.
Aww, boring! Alright, I will help.
Promise fulfilled. I promised you a necklace, and you have one.
Oh, I love when you're harsh! You're so macho! Turning on!
I adore you, honey! What did you decide to do with the beads?
Turns out I REALLY love gifts! You're so thoughtful, darling!
He did it by himself... Crispy...
She wants to take control of my abilities, just like that vile bastard Petrov did. But then my knight decapitated him!
It was terrible to realize that my body would outlive my mind! The doctors gave me no more than a year. The relentlessness of chemistry...
Careful, honey! If you press that, you'll set off problems you're not ready to handle!
Hey, watch out! Don't step on those papers, young man. I'm reading them!
It's like there's something... very important, but ghostly coming off of it... I can't understand or remember...
Survival bias? Maybe you shouldn't have been looking for something new, but studying the gaps instead.
The first capsule has been loaded.
Stop laughing! "Obvious..." Petrov is a bastard, that's what's obvious. Lay off, I need to think.
Ironically, time ran out on me. Though I'm inclined to believe that time doesn't exist, but is just a set of actions and thoughts that I'm now getting carried away with!
Getting a job in my field, and in such an important complex! Chemistry is the best!
It's easy for a cook to live in a swamp. Catch some frogs, get some firewood, and that's it! I know everything about frogs...
Go talk to that boring old man when you get to the surface. My scanners detected one of the beadies there. You can catch that too.
A childhood friend, heh. Go now. I ain't saying anymore—I already said too much. But it doesn't matter now.
And away we go! Check it out, it's comfortable.
For sure. You're so chipper, where are you from?
I see, no information from you then. I have to talk to Lebedev.
It was awful. Now it's the opposite. Age is the best stimulus for action, young man. And eternity is an excellent formula.
Try dropping a chandelier on it! Be careful: chandeliers explode!
A child of the array, darling. It's a ghost created by someone incredibly powerful.
Dead people can be pretty funny!
After the breach? Someone released the Septilegs. And then the Mads went crazy.
My final fantasy is for Captain Biggs or Sergeant Wedge to fly the Komar and say, "Look at what the Soviets did! It's breathtaking!"
Hang on, I don't recognize you.
That's commendable. Listen, I'd like to take a rest. Could you turn on the TVs in the complex? I want to watch the news.
Cute, right? It'll be a treat for you! Bear in mind that this is a consumable—keep it for when you really need it.
Should come in handy! This place is something else…
What a wonderful bug's life! Heh.
Perform the recombination, my boy! The Twins will be busy neutralizing NORA's pulse vortex. They won't be able to help you. But this also means that she can't stop you!
Drive that vicious old hag away, and the protocol disables itself!
Sorry, I'm in a hurry. Good luck!
I'm just a guest at the Lyogkaya.
You're confusing me for someone else. I'd better go.
Ha, yeah. Can't get rid of you...
I blabbed! You ran me ragged, you smooth-talker. Shame on you!
Of course. First of all, I remember the talking dead myself—it was quite recent. Anyway, I'm smart enough to add things up.
Tell me what you know about Katerina Nechaeva.
We've taken an incredible evolutionary leap with the Kollektiv, but my body didn't stop withering, and my brain didn't either.
I'd love to, but I still have some... business here.
I'll figure it out! I'm not a child!
I'm going to fix you now!
It's a secret, my grand cavalier! A woman must have her secrets. But don't worry about the teeth. I hope I'll never have to show them to you!
First you have to slice them, but don't cry..
I'm going to have a lovely necklace soon! Just a little more!
Soon I'll have a whole necklace of beadies!
The Teardrop you asked about has shown up here a few times. Its weak radiation proves that your wife is not completely gone.
That thing again. I came across it a few times while I was tracking Petrov down. I'm the only one who can see it. Even Charles didn't recognize what it was.
So? What have you done to me, crazy?
Save her? What for? Your wife's physical body is dead, and her consciousness is in pieces! Why would you need that?! Forget about her and enjoy what you have now!
The Mendeleev statue? Is there a button underneath it?
The Strekoza is fully operational, darling! You can fly it to the surface if you want to.
Aw fuck! Who let you back into this story?!
Shit, that's funny, crispy critters. And ridiculous! S-sorry.
Are you alright, my boy? Why did you go there alone? You could have waited for help!
That was two days ago! I'm sure it's all settled and nothing like that will happen again!
Well, so, what now? Anyone who dies in the Kollektiv just keeps rambling on like this forever?
And where can I go for a walk?
Okay, I put it together... Ah, nope.
Alright, the central capsule has been inserted. Great!
You have to turn off the generators! Think something up—you're smart!
I'm gifting them to you. They're beads, after all. We'll load them into you. For safety! You won't mind, will you?
Are you having fun, or did you slip? My Tarzan! You don't take care of yourself.
Now there are no restrictions! We're all Kollektiv!
Now we belong to each other! I synchronized your Voskhod module with my wave activity!
Now I have another little beady! How sweet of you, darling! Hurry up and put your gift in my chute!
Then into action, young man! And remember: the mind leads us!
But be careful: her puppets can be rather hostile.
There aren't any colorful ones here, just gray.
You said you'd figure it out yourself, my master!
You'll get hurt, darling! Be careful!
You'll pay for this betrayal! I will kill you!
You're a real man! I'm so happy with you, darling!
You found my little beady! Oh, sugar, you're so thoughtful!
You won't believe it, I dreamed about this one! What a wonderful little beady!
You're tireless, sugar! A real macho man!
My darling, you deceived me! You promised you wouldn't impose your will onto me!
Have you learned to read my private thoughts?!
You're making it up! How could you know anything about her?
You're simply the sweetest, my darling!
You must'a confused me with someone else, buddy.
I already have six little beadies! How wonderful!
She didn't have time to cipher the new schematic! I see the new sequence—I'm sending it to you! Rebuild the schematic!
Yeah. Endlessly. So, the Komar works. Good.
Yeah. I'd have to go to the surface anyway.
Yeah, I'll definitely give it to you. If these cute little beadies don't wipe the floor with me.
Yeah. Let's get to the chute.
That's what people say when they're trying to ensure their own comfort at the expense of others' suffering.
Uh-huh. Good ideas always come too late. Don't be upset, it happens to me all the time!
Beads in the morning, love in the evening! Or is it the other way around?
You left and that's the last we saw of you. And then she finished everyone off. Bitch. Sorry.
Ha, funny you say that: "wouldn't dream of it."
Ha ha! And who do I love?
Ha ha! And Petrov planted it on the dead man. It's so obvious!
Ha ha! Is that even possible? I trust you completely, my darling! Talk to the old hag. Then return.
He he! You're like a cute, clumsy kitten. Who's my sweet little thing? So wet!
Hm. Unlikely. Guests don't wear that kind of gear.
The Komar is good! A miracle! The future of aviation! Vertical takeoff, supersonic... The F-100 doesn't stand a chance!
Why can't you just act normally from the beginning?
What didn't you like about the Kollektiv?
What's Granny Zina done to rub you the wrong way?
The fourteenth is in—just a few more!
So why didn't this Kollektiv help you?
Well, I'm sure time will tell.
What did she do? Ha ha! My naive Sergey!
What happened there? Who attacked Sechenov?
What do you know about her?
So there were... accidents at the Facility.
So, the cook just slipped and fell—no big deal! It's just us here!
The experiment failed. So I guess it wasn't.
NORA was able to reconfigure the recombination schematic! That's why you couldn't put it together!
NORA, so what is that Teardrop?
NORA, have you detected radiation from another bead on the surface?
The electromagnetic radiation will keep the beads from merging!
L, that you? Man, I don't have anymore. That wasn't enough?
This little beady is also painted a special color! It's just gray!
This shit is too strong! I won't last!
The Komar! I've flown one of these. Is it operative?
That's a Strekoza. I saw them flying on the surface. Did you also deactivate this one?
It's a storm of our passion, honey!
That was the last one. All ready for recombination.
What's this chaos?! NORA! Turn this insane crap off!
They're the reason I can't fully block that boring old man's control signals!
It's rational, at the very least, but call it what you want.
It's our home! We're going to protect it together.
That doesn't matter! I have the right to choose how I want to live!
The recombination schematic. It's all so simple, clearly! I can't make heads or tails of it, damn it!
That won't happen! You're going to die!
Eh... Either way, if I'd had doubts about the Kollektiv before its launch or after the breach, now I'm sure: it's the worst thing that has happened to mankind.
I'm ecstatic! You're such a sweetheart!
I keep thinking... How did Filatova fasten his head on?
I'm so far removed from all that, sugar. The petty problems of unworthy people hold no interest for me!
I said you wouldn't like it, honey!
I'm here, honey! I'm sorry, I was wrapped up in introspection. Personal growth is very important!
I'm a person! I can certainly make things up, but I learned this information from the Teardrop. But you don't care, you hardened bastard! Go ahead, erase my identity!
I can't figure out who it is, but I feel that the Teardrop is searching for something you threw away.
I feel it inside of me! Turns out I love gifts. Just fifteen more!
I changed my mind. Your way of life hurts others.
I'm glad you like it, darling!
I'm a realist who's just spent a week trying to get out of this nightmare.
I'm the best "chick," sweetheart! Don't offend me. I have teeth!
I'm going to launch the recombination now.
I'm mad with excitement! When? When will you give them to me?
I'm also... an employee. Just in another department.
I want to remember my own life. And the only clues I have are that flying goo and a possibly-alive Katya. But right now, I have nothing.
Me?! I didn't throw shit away, I've never even had anything. Wait...

Surveying monocycle robot GMC-69 with multipurpose prospecting functions.  Vatrushka's complex system of cameras and sensors is capable of high-precision tachymetric surveying.  Thanks to the built-in seismograph, Vatrushka can detect mineral deposits, solve hydrogeological and geotechnical problems, and carry out seismic microzoning.

The large-scale surveyor robot HOG-7 collects rare plants and minerals.  Despite its impressive size, Hedgie can switch to the Tumbleweed mode, accelerating and retracting its long limbs to reach speeds of up to 50 km/h.  Hedgie's limbs feature special drills and a compressor that can easily pick up valuable resources from the Earth's surface. Thanks to detailed cartographical data stored on an in-built hard drive, Hedgie can gather and instantly analyze available topographic and geodetic materials. The HOG-8 model will be equipped with state-of-the-art wireless transmission technology.

The large MA-9 robot is used for construction and welding work.   Belyash can easily carry a load of half a ton. Its average service life amounts to at least 20 years. Unlike the MA-7 and MA-8 that did manual or semi-automatic welding, MA-9 is equipped with the argon-arc welding technology. It is expected that MA-10 will finally feature laser welding.  Thanks to its steel-titanium alloy shell, Belyash can operate even in extreme conditions, at ambient temperatures between -75 and +75 °C. Its chassis is based on a chimpanzee skeleton, and MA-9 can climb steep surfaces and construction beams just like its prototype. Comrade Abalakov, a renowned mountain climber, took part in the development of Belyash's hands.
This is the miniature observation helicopter ORB-I7. The ORB can monitor traffic, supervise law and order in public venues, and swiftly respond when trespassers are detected.

The rotation speed of the mower blades starts at 540 rpm.  Use extreme caution when switching it on to prevent accidents.

The MFU-68 robot was designed for the needs of animal husbandry and serves as a shepherd for cows, sheep, goats, and so on.  The Laborer traverses rough terrain with ease and is immune to the harsh weather conditions of the Far North or Mongolian steppes. To control a large herd, Laborers can join into groups.  The MFU-68/L variation is an improved model of the Laborer equipped with a 40-cm circular blade for felling trees at logging sites. The Laborer shows good results when paired with the MTU-7 Bumblebee log transporter. It is resistant to weather conditions and can withstand temperatures as low as -45 °C.

The little Sprout is a link between the worlds of botany and zoology and the future of food production.  Featuring a mixture of plant and animal proteins, it is the unprocessed food of the future. Cultivating Sprouts is a humane alternative to animal husbandry: no longer will millions of cows and chickens have to be slaughtered on a daily basis to feed Soviet citizens. Better yet, Sprouts can move about independently: healthy food will find its way to the hungry on its own!

The WSP-9 light transport drone performs deliveries and can repair any technical object, including other robots connected to the Kollektiv ecosystem.  Pchela has increased maneuverability and high speed of flight due to its small size, but cannot lift loads heavier than 25 kg.  Pchela repairs objects using a flexible cable that can be secured in any position and holds the Polymer arc welding wire.

The RAF-9 robot can produce, operate, and maintain various kinds of equipment.  The Engineer can operate basic metal-cutting, woodworking, and stone-cutting machinery as well as complex computerized devices. All Engineer models feature protocols for optimal repair of simple non-robotic equipment.  Engineers are used not only in production but also in everyday life: the robot can easily work as a janitor, electrician, locksmith, or plumber, freeing its owners from the drudgery of daily chores.

The medium universal copter MUC-1 is mainly used to transport cargo over short distances.  Drofa easily reaches speeds of up to 50 km/h and can carry loads of several hundred kilograms.  In addition to cargo transportation, Drofa is used in the agricultural industry. Thanks to the unique shape of the blades which operate on the principle of the Archimedes screw, it can transport water for remote field and pasture irrigation.

The TER/A1 robot performs basic administrative and advisory functions.  This anthropomorphic robotic assistant is based on the VOV/A6 and designed with the participation of Comrade Tereshkova, the actress, cosmonaut, and decorated Soviet hero. The TER/A1 robot is the most advanced product of Facility 3826, addressing the shortcomings of the previous generation and introducing many new features such as voice modulation and self-repair.  Tereshkova is one of the few robots independent from the Kollektiv ecosystem: it still reacts only to verbal human commands. Perhaps after the launch of Kollektiv everyone will be able to enjoy a virtual Tereshkova of their own.

The VOV-A6 robot helps scientists carry out experiments and tests in research facilities.  The Lab Tech was given human shape to prevent negative psychological effects on human employees. Originally, the Lab Tech shell was made of aluminum alloys and plastic, but after the groundbreaking biological Polymer discovery all latest models are shipped in a cutting-edge lifelike hull.  Its anthropomorphic hand prostheses have over 100 sensors, providing the high precision required in handling hazardous substances.

The flying Mutant is the surprise result of symbiosis between a Sprout and a human corpse.  When a Sprout finds a dead body, it grows its stems through the mouth and nose, penetrating the brain and taking control of the corpse's motor functions in under a minute. The hybrid is fully submissive to the Sprout and can either move on two legs or hover on propeller-like leaves.

The scary Plyusch is the endoskeleton of an experimental bionic creature, consisting of an animated blob of polymeric muscles with an implanted dog brain.   The Plyusch usually moves on its hind legs, but can run on all fours at the speed of a wild wolf. The biorobot can extend its limbs to several times their original length and jump dozens of meters high.

The heavy-duty land robot loader NA-T256 carries weights up to 2.5 tons and is used for complex repair works.  Natasha is widely used on construction sites all over the USSR. The enormous engine power and battery capacity allows up to 24 hours of continuous operation on a single battery charge. Without Natasha the construction of Dneprovskaya, Kuibyshevskaya, and Stalingradskaya hydroelectric power plants would have been impossible, not to mention finishing the Baikonur Cosmodrome ahead of schedule.  Some of the Natasha models are equipped with adjusted rocket engines, developed under the guidance of Comrade Korolev, which allow the heavy robot to climb to proportionate heights, assuming the safety precautions are observed: no people without protection gear can be near Natasha during the take off.

The many-limbed Dewdrop is a heavy bionic creature, a massive blob of biological Polymer muscle, wrapped in synthetic membrane that both helps the robot to maintain shape and facilitates transportation on an industrial scale.  The biorobot will be used in the mining industry: not only can it lift heavy loads, it also performs precise borehole drilling with its mechanical laser unit.

The MED-6 medical robot can replace a nurse and perform different procedures from drawing blood to carrying out diagnostic surgeries.   The Medic is based on the MFU-68 Laborer chassis. The main difference between the two are the Medic's larger legs, which are required to treat patients both on the floor and in hospital beds. The Medic's head unit is equipped with a multifunctional appliance for routine medical operations such as blood sampling.  Its replaceable tanks contain various biological Polymer solutions, such as anesthetic and antiseptic liquids.

The light universal copter LUC-1 performs various tasks in the agro-industrial and livestock complex, watching the crops and pastures in the Soviet collective farms.  Unlike the larger Drofa model, the Owl is smaller and has lower lifting power, but makes up for it by featuring better mobility: Owls can reach speeds of up to 75 km/h. Several Owls can team up to transport heavy loads.  The main purpose of the Owl is to keep a watchful eye on cattle.

Alexey Lebedev is an electrical engineer and energy specialist and the founder of Soviet computing technology. He was the head of the All-Russian Electronics Institute's automation department and the director of the Institute of Precision Mechanics and Computing Technology. Lebedev created the first electronic analog computing machine in the country in order to solve ordinary differential equations that are frequently encountered in energy-related fields. The first small electronic calculation machine in the Soviet Union and Continental Europe was also developed under his leadership. He is the head of a top-secret AoC department, but, thanks to his friend and colleague Privalov, he has been able to free himself from administrative duties and continue studying the quantum entanglement of radio waves. The Radio of the Future is his most cherished and inimitable creation.

Dr. Sechenov is a neurosurgeon, roboticist, inventor, and philanthropist. He began his career studying collective intelligence at the Soviet Academy of Medical Sciences' Brain Research Center, where he hoped to engineer a perfect way of life for the communal cities of the future. He worked on the ManKind Project before the war, but dedicated himself to studying the Polymer after it was discovered. After World War II he was put in charge of a robotics program designed to make up for the country's significant lack of human resources and took over Facility 3826 on Comrade Stalin's personal order. Once Soviet robots had been distributed throughout the world, Comrade Sechenov become the Minister of Industry. His revolutionary discovery of the Polymer's capacity for mimetic adaption made it possible to inject this extraordinarily promising new technology into human tissues. This laid the framework for what would later become Kollektiv 2.0, a merging of humans and machines into a single neural network capable of fundamentally transforming and improving the everyday lives of not just Soviet citizens, but the entire world.

Despite his parents' and teachers' expectations, Petelka did not become a famous physicist. Although he certainly had the potential, the young man's exceptional mind and fantastic imagination ultimately allowed his reach to exceed his grasp. Comrade Petelka learned about robots from a newspaper article even before the war and never stopped fantasizing about them. Petelka did end up becoming a physicist, although he was never famous. He worked with Comrade Filimonenko on a cold Polymer synthesis project, was an excellent robot configuration technician at the Maya Plisetskaya Theater, and even made his way to the secret departments of the AoC, where he truly felt his "insignificance before the vastness of the cosmos."  "I understand this world perfectly. We're all just grains of sand in an ocean of electrical connections," Comrade Petelka declared before retiring from science, effective immediately. But he did not leave the Facility. Having returned to his duties configuring robots and servicing the theater's electrical grid, Petelka is, perhaps more than any other Soviet citizen, eagerly anticipating the Kollektiv 2,0 update that will utterly efface the boundary between human cognition and the capabilities of robots.  "We're all just electric currents, just ones and zeroes" is a favorite phrase of Petelka's, who often spends his free time in the theater's coat check room observing his favorite robot, the coat check girl.

Nikolai Vavilov is a geneticist and botanist. He led botanical expeditions to Western Europe, Asia, Africa, North America, and South America that have enabled him to identify the original sites of the morphogenesis of plants. Vavilov laid the foundation for the study of plant immunity and discovered the law of the homological series in the hereditary variation of organisms. A German scientist of Jewish descent, Stockhausen worked as a doctor in Berlin during the war. He lived through the first outbreaks of the Brown Plague and was later saved by Soviet soldiers. Prior to his infection, he had an incredible memory—a fact his coworkers could attest to—but lost this ability after the onset of the illness and never demonstrated it again (although he does not regret the loss).  Thanks to his scientific and organizational talents, Stockhausen's career enjoyed a startlingly rapid ascent. He was recruited to the Facility in order to fill a quota for scientists from the German Soviet Socialist Republic and quickly earned Sechenov's respect. Despite his German pedantry and a certain degree of snobbishness, he remains one of the best-known—and best-liked—members of the Facility 3826 team. He is perfectly capable of speaking Russian without an accent, but chooses to "sound German" in order to remind people of his origins.

Comrade Lastochkin is not a traditional theater director. Better known as "Stefan," Lastochkin has had a stunning career, starting out as an office manager and becoming the head of what is perhaps the most famous theater in the world. In less than a year, unique performances such as "The Binding Screws of Friendship," "In the Vice of Passion," and the modern classic "Electric Origins" have become sensations among fans of avant-garde art. However, his narcissism, shady dealings, and despotic management style have set many theater employees at odds with the ambitious new director.

Организатор и участник ботанико-агрономических экспедиций, охвативших большинство континентов (кроме Австралии и Антарктиды), в ходе которых выявил древние очаги формообразования культурных растений. Создал учение о мировых центрах происхождения культурных растений[6]. Обосновал учение об иммунитете растений, открыл закон гомологических рядов в наследственной изменчивости организмов. Внёс существенный вклад в разработку учения о биологическом виде. Под руководством Вавилова была создана крупнейшая в мире коллекция семян культурных растений. Он заложил основы системы государственных испытаний сортов полевых культур. Сформулировал принципы деятельности главного научного центра страны по аграрным наукам, создал сеть научных учреждений в этой области

Vortex automatic trains will soon crisscross the entire country, extending to even the most distant reaches of the Soviet Union.

Date: January 12, 1955 From: Pavlov Complex Manager I. Pavlov To: Pavlov Cultural Archivist V. Nikitin  Progress by leaps and bounds has become typical of humanity in this challenging 20th century. Against the background of tremendous inequality, breakthroughs in science and technology can seem not just astonishing, but even insulting. But this is a sociological and political matter. Much like the pseudo-scientific fears voiced when the railroads were being built, when the suggestion was actually made that the sight of the landscape whizzing by at 50 kilometers per hour would drive passengers mad, I am beset by similar predictions. Just 25 years ago more than half of all Soviet citizens were illiterate. Today, we are flying into space. What awaits us tomorrow? Will we have time to catch our breath before our next great leap?

Date: October 15, 1954 From: Pavlov Debate Club President N. Azarova to: archive terminal  Speaker: When I give talks in the Soviet Union and allied countries, I am often asked whether it makes sense to focus scientific progress on making fundamental changes to the human race. We could, for example, teach people to change the properties of their skin in order to make it more resistant to heat or cold, or regrow lost limbs like certain reptiles, or control their biochemistry on a basic level. In other words, to rephrase a well-known thesis, should we strive for "evolution in the individual?"  From the room: skeptical laughter  Speaker: My answer is "no." I admit that this is a defeatist attitude. But my objection does not lie in some bourgeois conception of man as the pinnacle of creation. We have access to powerful technology, and yet we should not alter ourselves to suit our environment. This would be a step backwards. Instead, we must perfect science in order to fully subjugate nature itself, whether it be here on Earth, or somewhere else.

You want to know if you can buy a lottery ticket knowing that it will win, or avoid a nuclear holocaust. Am I right? It's not that simple. One day we intercepted an emergency message about the launch of nuclear missiles in 1976... I was horrified. The future DOES NOT EXIST YET. Please remember that. All we can hear is an echo of an infinite quantumized multivariance and extract the most frequently repeated tendencies from it. What we will actually see tomorrow is entirely in our hands.

Topic: The Atomic Heart Project Speaker: Dr. Dmitry Sechenov  Welcome, Comrades. In 1951, the capitalist imperialism of the United States, consumed by hatred and envy for the Soviet Union's magnificent scientific achievements, declared the launch of the global Energy for All program. In essence, this program is just as hypocritical as the capitalist system itself. Hiding behind a facade of lofty ideals, the capitalists strive for worldwide hegemony, the suppression of all independence other than their own, and the eradication of those who do not share their values.  At first glance, Energy for All seems incredibly noble: fifty nuclear power stations will be constructed throughout the United States in order to provide every American citizen with cheap and available electricity. But the United States' capitalist regime is, as always, hiding its true face, twisted into the beastly grin of imperialism, behind a mask of magnanimity. In addition to these power stations, the United States is also secretly building a network of underground silos and hangars for launching nuclear missiles and housing strategic bombers armed with nuclear bombs.  The Americans' goal is simple: once the Soviet Union believes their claims of peace and friendship, it will let down its guard, and the American military machine will strike, destroying the Soviet Union and the entire communist way of life with a cowardly sneak attack! But the Soviet Union isn't one to sit on its hands and wait while our enemies regroup and swell their ranks, hiding nuclear weapons underground where we cannot eliminate them from orbit. Nor is the Soviet Union one to back down or run from another nation's might. In response to the American threat, Facility 3826 has developed its own project designed not only to protect the Soviet Union, but also to rid the world once and for all of the very possibility of such a bloodbath. The president of the United States once called Energy for All America's "atomic heart." Given the profound guile and hypocrisy of American capitalism, this name reflects the essence of the global threat developed by the United States all too well. For this reason, our project, which will counteract the Americans' deadly machinations, has co-opted their leader's metaphor. Our Atomic Heart will return honestly and integrity to America!  The Atomic Heart project is made up of several sequential steps:  - Design and build civilian robots with no weapons or other signs of a potential military application. These robots have been designed to be independent of their software. Any owner can install any software onto them they like. On the outside, the robots seems to be perfectly harmless, safe, and friendly. But in reality, they are equipped with highly effective hand-to-hand combat techniques and can use civilian equipment as lethal weapons.  - Stage two of this project requires that Soviet civilian robots be seen by the entire world as humanitarian goods. We have already implemented this strategy via the United Nations. Since receiving the status of humanitarian goods, Soviet robots have begun to spread throughout the entire world free of charge, which has given a powerful impetus to the further development of the Atomic Heart project. Profit-hungry American capitalists are flooding their country with our robots. A free robotic workforce is the dream of every capitalist usurper, and none of them has hesitated to obtain as many Soviet robots as possible.  - During stage three, the Soviet Union has made obtaining free robots as easy as possible for our foreign customers. American businesses, for one, have already imported over one hundred million Soviet civilian robots of various models. Many of these are used at facilities related to Energy for All, i.e. American power stations and missile silos. There, our robots, on which American special forces have installed their own software, maintain, service, and operate nuclear facilities. The first objective of the Atomic Heart project has thus been accomplished.  - During the final phase of the project, civilian robots will be switched form civilian operation to combat mode. They will then capture all key components of the infrastructure of the United States. This will become possible with the launch of Kollektiv 2.0, which will unite all Soviet robots into a unified Neuropolymer network that requires no radio signals, digital protocols, or other electronics. All Soviet robots will be able to receive and successfully carry out our commands. Their attack will be sudden, and it will happen everywhere, all at once, down to the second. The enemy will be taken completely by surprise, and they will be eradicated. The American working class will be liberated from the oppression of global capitalism, and the very notion of capitalism will be lost in the waters of Lethe.  The launch of Kollektiv 2.0 is only two months away. In just two months, a new, progressive human race will toss capitalism into the dustbin of history, cast off the tyrants' yoke, and begin its march into the future. The world will never be the same, comrades!

Neutron star When a star goes nova and dies, it can transform into a quickly revolving neutron star. We believe that neutron stars within a strong magnetic field could emit similar strange signals. Blitzar A quickly revolving neutron star that cannot bear its own weight, so it collapses very quickly and transforms into a black hole. Human error The imperfections inherent in available equipment (even Soviet equipment), human error when calculating data—either of these things could lead to an inaccurate interpretation.

Bykov: And now you're gone, Professor. What have you done?! I was supposed to learn from you, but all I ever got from you was scorn. My self-worth all depended on you, and now... oh well. I've still got bullets, I can still fight my way through science. And I stole the box from your office with your favorite music inside. Just so I don't forget, I hid the music box in a safe, the one with the positive password, not the negative one. What will I ever accomplish if I can't even keep a couple of safes straight?! The dog! The dog has the positive one!
In the Soviet Union, we're the gods

Vavilov: Congratulations on your promotion, Comrade Zolotukhin! Deputy director of the Vavilov Complex is a very important position. Right now our primary goal is to provide the Soviet people with sustenance, which requires great attention, but very, very soon mankind's first steps into outer space will begin right here as well. As an outstanding botanist, you will be tasked with overseeing the creation of entire systems of plants designed to terraform the surfaces of other worlds! Comrade Sechenov and I had a talk earlier, and we're both delighted that you have joined our team. Ahem... you see, Vic, we do not just want to plant corn on the Moon — we want to take a bite of a bigger apple, on Mars.

Inspired artist: So, I just woke up, and I had a brilliant idea for an exhibit! Well, it's not really an exhibit, it's more like an experience. Anyway, here it is: visitors walk into a dark room, grab a Chirper, put on headphones, and hear something like... read this, Tereshkova.  Tereshkova: Imagine you're in a beautiful green field, surrounded by an endless forest that stretches from one horizon to the other. You hear a brook burbling nearby, birds singing and puppies, lots of puppies...  Inspired artist: End recording. So while a woman's voice is describing this landscape, some Pchelas create a holographic image of it all around them! What's the point, you ask? Well, to be honest, I don't know yet... but it's an awesome idea! I'll just have to explain why I woke up next to that Tereshkova...  Tereshkova: I am the perfect woman. I am present, I am at peace... A flowing stream, an endless forest, a forever blue sky in touch with my inner goddess.  Inspired artist: Turn off, dammit!

Verbitsky: Comrade Ismailov, this is Verbitsky. I just saw an unknown employee pull a military Polymer container out of a truck and put it in the trunk of his white car. He looked frightened, like he was running from something. I walked up to him and told him to stop, but he just floored it and drove away from the train station. So what I want to know is... hey, what's that? Holy shit...

Goopy electrician: So what if she's a robot? People have never been nice to me. But she is. The way she looks at me... It's like there's a stream of pure energy in her eyes. And she understands me. Better than any girl ever has. Anyway, I've made up my mind. I'm proposing to her tomorrow.  Angry voice: What the fuck are you doing here, Vasilitch? Are you working here or not?  Vasilitch: Shit... I'm coming!

Indignant male voice: Hey Stepan, this is nuts. You've gone too far here…  Stepan: Stefan! My name is Stefan, not Stepan! And what exactly have I gone overboard from, Maris-Rudolph? The ship of decency? The only ship of decency we have to worry about is our patrons' wishes! What do we always say in the Soviet Union?  Maris-Rudolph: Huh?  Lastochkin: "All in the name of man, for the good of man!" And these men need to walk out of here with smiles on their faces!  Maris-Rudolph: I dunno...  Lastochkin: Oh yes you do! You're a fine artist, and you've got a bright future ahead of you. Don't get in your own way... Or the robots will push you to the sidelines of history! Okay, you can go now. Shoo!

Excited female voice: I stopped by the archive yesterday, and everything there is so automated! We won't have to work at all pretty soon. We'll just sit there listening to music. Here's a piece! Robots can't appreciate it the way we do.  (radio of the Future music plays)

Are you with the delegation? I haven't seen you before.  Yeah, I'm... uhh... I'm new here. I was sent here by... umm... I… I forget the name.  Comrade Lastochkin?  Yes, that's right! It… it was him. He told me you'd show me around, Comrade...  You can call me Olga. Have a seat. Since you're the Boss' protegé, I suppose, your visit's been paid for.  Paid? Uh... I don't understand. It's… it's my first time here, actually. He, he. What are you, ugh... what are you gonna show me?  It's more like… a performance. A special program... for special visitors.  Huh… Is it a dance?  Oh, aren't you sweet? I like newcomers, you're so innocent! I guess you could call it a dance... yeah... let's call it "lap dance."  (ZIP!)  Whoa! Hey! W-What are you doing, Comrade Olga?!  Huh, silly. Don't shout... yet.  Oh... oh... wow, what a performance! Oh…
A brilliant idea for an exhibit! (not really)

Pissed-off voice: You're fired! Fuck you and the horse you rode in on, Pestsov! You've been tracking radio waves from space for three years and waiting for aliens?! That was a goddamn microwave oven! I hope you get killed by a meteorite, you fucking asshole! I've had it up to here with you!

Gruff adult voice: Everything's fine... take it easy now... the bosses know what they're doing.  Diffident younger voice: Diman, I haven't even been here a week yet, and I've already seen enough corpses for a lifetime! I thought this place was gonna be a regular clinic... I had no idea it was like this!  Diman: Ha ha... didn't the fact that this place is a secret complex tip you off? You're a little green to be a guard, especially at a hospital. Listen, we're not butchers like those scientists — we're not here to kill people. We just make sure no one runs off. It's fine, really.

Gruff male voice: What's that s'posed to mean, ""it's hot?"" You're hot, eh?! Ya oughtta try going to the Urals and being a steelworker, even for half shifts! That'd make a man of ya, I tell ya! But look at 'im: instead he's over there with his pretty flowers, bitchin' about the heat. We Krakotovs don't give a goddamn about no heat! Ain't nothin' gonna stop us! We'll hop right into an oven or a volcano at the drop of a hat. So don't come whimperin' to me, bub. Once they update Kollektiv, everything'll be hunky-dory. And if someone starts bitchin', they ain't worth shit! Ha ha ha!
Gourmand: Alexandra, could I have some chicken Kyiv and mashed potatoes, please? Oh, and a pickle. Just one.

Female tour guide: Don't worry, Dina! I'm actually glad they've got the Tereshkovas giving tours now instead of us. We still get paid, and we get to take a nice vacation. Sounds good to me. My hubby and I are heading to Yalta to visit the family. I'm tired, you know? There are more and more tourists coming every day, even from Moscow. The adults ask question after question. And the kids? Och. They go nuts when they see all the gadgets here. Yesterday two little boys almost fell into the Polymer whale. Can you imagine? A lot of things fall into that whale, actually. Yevgeny the janitor says you can find all kinds of stuff in there.

Village fashionista: Can I get a 9:00 appointment, Nina? I'm gonna take a day off! Lyudmila got one of those amazing Poly hairstyles for her wedding. Could you do that for me too, pretty please? You know, the kind where it's one style in the morning, and then it's different in the evening, and the color changes and everything? Everybody's gonna be there for the Kollektiv update — all our bosses, and maybe even some foreigners! I don't wanna look all frumpy... oh, and grab me some Poly nail polish too, okay? I want my nails to change with my mood! Polymers sure are amazing for beauty stuff, huh?
Bykov's diary—the dog with the positive password

Good-natured male voice: Mikhalych, I'm gonna go grab some lunch. You want anything?  Mikhalych: Don't do me any favors. I marched all the way to Berlin in my day. I can make it to the cafeteria, thank you very much.  Good-natured male voice: Oh, chill out! Just trying to help. You know all the mashed potatoes'll be gone and then I'll have to hear all about it.  Mikhalych: Eh, go on. I'll catch up to ya. Hell, I'll prolly get there first.  Good-natured male voice: Whatever...  Mikhalych: These people... what, I'm not a man anymore 'cuz I lost my leg? I don't need nobody to baby me. I can get there myself without their "help." I don't want pity, I want respect, dammit! I'll be runnin' laps around you yet, mark my words!

Good-natured male voice: Okay, this is VDNH. Comrade journalist.  Foreign journalist: Hmm... I expected something a little more... grandiose...  Secret tour guide: Yeah, everybody thinks that. Kindly male voice: About that doll, Vladlena...I understand that your toys are aren't really for young children, but it'd be a shame to throw them away, and I feel a little weird about keeping them myself. Anyway, they found a puppy by the Facility gate two weeks ago with that doll in its mouth. Maybe it got lost, or maybe it was just abandoned. It seemed like a fine dog. But it wouldn't give up the doll, it just kept carrying it around in its mouth. We thought about using it as a guard dog, but it was just too nasty. Anyway, we ended up giving it to Pavlov. They love dogs there, and they won't hurt it. But I didn't know what to do with the doll, so I thought I might give it to your museum. I just feel too sad looking at it...

Female voice: Have a seat, Mikhail. I just need to finish my work, and then I'll help you with that report. Lab Tech #84, bring Comrade Koltsov some tea. I'll be with you in a second, okay?

Did he even know what madness is?

Zolotukhin: They say "Monday begins on Saturday" but I'd like you to really take the weekend off. As you know, national polymerization is happening throughout the Soviet Union on Monday the 13th, and our executive leaders want us to put together a team of volunteers for the upcoming celebrations. Anybody who works on the 11th or the 12th will get a reprimand, not a bonus. Have a great weekend.

Zolotukhin: Smoking-related issues have been especially intense since the war, and Comrade Stalin just added fuel to the fire by making pipes look stylish. Now we've ended up with an unhealthy nationwide addiction. I suggest introducing a special kind of tobacco to the market. It contains almost no nicotine and is completely free of harmful tar, and, most importantly, it gradually introduces an aversion to smoking. It's cheap to make and can easily replace ordinary tobacco. We could help two thirds of Soviet smokers kick the habit in just five years.

Zolotukhin: Comrade Vavilov, the graduate students have come up with a new pastime: they're playing tic-tac-toe on the breeding beds. One of them plants corn, and the other plants tomatoes, and they go back and forth like that. I was going to chew them out, but then I realized it's actually a decent little game. It's like a whole new kind of chess. What do you think about opening an agricultural gaming club?

Zolotukhin: Attention all coworkers: please listen to this Chirper and leave it where it is. Its purpose is to remind everyone not to take plant specimens home under any circumstances, including seemingly harmless ones. Flowers from the labs may have built-in genetic traits that will have a negative effect on your quality of life. If it's grown in a lab, it stays in a lab. Period.
