A scientist is approaching.  AI Betsy: Goddammit...  Lab tech: What the hell? Stop recording.
Engineers need to follow the dress code!

Foreign journalist: Why does this say ""Gods of Labor?"" I thought you didn't care about gods or religion in the Soviet Union.  Secret tour guide: We don't care about the opium of the masses, but there are gods, and then there are gods. Take Prometheus the god of fire who brought light and warmth.  Foreign journalist: Prometheus was actually a titan, not a god...  Secret tour guide: Hey, watch your step, okay? So what's a god? Somebody who protects you, who teaches you how to live, who's wiser and smarter than everyone else. In the Soviet Union, we're the gods. Everybody who works for the good of others, who brings new knowledge to the world. The man of science and labor is the new god of planet Earth — homo futurum!  Foreign journalist: Uh... Thank you.  Secret tour guide: Don't forget your camera again. Okay, next question?
Comrade Stockhausen's schemes, or "I'll scratch your back..."

Computer voice: For visitors: a standard Chelomey Design Bureau office. This is a recreation of a standard office used by Chelomey Design Bureau employees. The finest minds in the Soviet Union work day and night in offices just like this one to help build a glorious future for us all. As you can see, every aspect of this office is designed to make our employees' jobs easier. The pleasant gray walls help them focus on work, and the lack of sharp corners reduces the risk of injury. The desks, shelves, and bookcases are constructed from an aluminum alloy, making them durable, but still light and easy to move. It doesn't matter what task a Facility employee is working on — whether they're studying complex microchips, working on biological species, or performing surgery, they can be confident that everything in their environment will help them achieve great things.

Computer voice: The Chelomey Design Bureau, named after its director Dr. Vladimir Chelomey, is the brain of the entire Facility. Chelomey's engineering labs and manufacturing facilities are where Facility employees first built the robots that have allowed the Soviet Union to become the undisputed world leader in science and technology. Every day millions of robots, from simple lawn mowers to Tereshkovas that are indistinguishable from human beings, help Soviet citizens and the entire world march toward a brilliant future.

Computer voice: Welcome, visitor! This is one of Chelomey's latest innovations. It's called a PEAR. The PEAR is a communications terminal that can be used to send text, video, and audio messages and store personal information for every Facility employee. In the near future there will be PEARs in every home in the Soviet Union, allowing our citizens to correspond with each other, obtain information, and exchange it with anyone, no matter where they are.

Ministry of Culture curator: Listen up, everyone. I took a look at some recordings of your tours. Why are they so boring? ""Rafiks are this and that kind of robot, yada yada yada."" And then you get all technical... There are kids there, you know? Young Pioneers, Octobrists. You gotta keep them entertained! Watch this: this is robot Rafik! He's really nice and friendly. He might be a little on the chubby side, but he's really neat! Or... I dunno... he kicks ass!  Confused tour guide: You want us to say ""ass"" in front of the kids?  Ministry of Culture curator: You know what I mean! Don't say ""he kicks ass,"" say... I dunno, something else! Make the tours fun! Let the little buggers crawl all over the bots, let them ride them or something, I dunno! They're safe and fun! We need to get kids interested in robots, not put them to sleep!

Ministry of Culture curator: This is a robot vacuum or "robo-vacuum." It's totally bad ass! Just look at it moving in slow motion! Okay, let's see... It's got an elongated body and very narrow shoulders, which allows it to suck up dirt in almost any area. Just look at all the trash everywhere! But the robo-vacuum doesn't give a crap, it just destroys all that junk and keeps on sucking up the dirt. Uh-oh, someone spilled a bucket of paint on the robo-vacuum! But the robo-vacuum acts like it doesn't even notice it got sticky paint all over it. Look at that fucker — it'll just clean everything up, and it'll just keep on sucking! Get it, Dmitry? That's how we need to open our fellow citizens' eyes to the amazing things we make here at the Facility, not your lame old "the Zaporozhia Automotive Factory presents model ROZGDFG-20 or 40 or whatever..." It's boring to death.

Lastochkin: We are pleased to welcome you to our roboticized theater! It's the first of its kind in the world, and it's based on your design! I've made a few little tweaks here and there, of course. Comrade Sechenov, Comrade Zakharov, please follow me!  Zakharov: What a wonderful evening, Dmitry! What an incredible performance! I propose a toast to Voskhod — science has never been so close to, eh... triumph!

Lastochkin: The ballerinas' training is proceeding magnificently! We just need to show them the proper ballet positions. It's a shame they aren't connected to the primary neural network — just imagine what we could teach them! And, most importantly, no Polymer injections whatsoever. Truly fantastical women! Just say the name of a position, and that's it! And it doesn't have to be a ballet position either...

Lastochkin: Our prima ballerina isn't ready yet. We need to tighten up her servos — she's flopping around like a rag doll on stage. Get me the technician! I tell you, these robot ballerinas are just as bad as their human counterparts. I can't work under these conditions!

Lastochkin: Hi, Comrade Yelizarova, Lastochkin here. Listen, we seem to have gotten off on the wrong foot. You think I'm a con artist, and I called you a frigid old bat... but we were just kidding around, right? Maybe you can meet me halfway. The VDNH should really have an exhibit for our theater, with ballerinas, stage backdrops, and recorded performances. The Lastochkin Theater... I mean, the Plisetskaya Theater is the crown jewel of Facility 3826, and everybody knows it. If there's any way we can resolve this issue in a more... mutually beneficial way, just say the word, okay, doll? Stefan Lastochkin's got your back.

Lastochkin: Comrade Zolotukhin, my dear colleague... We haven't really had a chance to get acquainted yet, but I assure you, if you attend our theater under my guidance, you'll never forget the name Lastochkin! I've got a little favor to ask of you: could you send us a few of those fascinating flowers of yours? The theater just isn't green enough, and it could use a little more exoticism, if you catch my drift. A little bird told me you've got some creeping bushes now — I'd love to have a dozen of those to wow my VIPs with. I'll make it worth your while, of course. Sincerely yours, Stefan Lastochkin

Lastochkin: This is my chance! It's a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity! No more artists' clubs, no more orders from on high, no more memos or approval processes! Just take it, make it, and let it be! And it's going to be... great! The name of Lastochkin, the world's first robo-director, will resound throughout the world! Hmm... robo-director... it's kinda shitty. I need to come up with a better title... and a better name. ""Stepan"" just isn't me! Most importantly, I need to keep the bosses happy, and then no one will say boo! Holy smokes!

Engineer: This is the engineer speaking. The system is down. I can't stop the train. Our speed is increasing. We're trying...  Junior engineer: You need to drop it, Andrey. Right now!  Engineer: Have you lost your mind?  Junior engineer: No! If we go any further, if we keep increasing speed, we're gonna slam right into the village! We'll kill a ton of people! And if we don't...  Engineer: Then we'll kill ourselves, Igor!  Junior engineer: We're gonna die anyway! We'll just take fewer people with us. Come on, engineer!  Engineer: Okay, I get it. This is the engineer speaking. We've made an emergency decision to derail the train to avoid more casualties... oh no... hang on, Igor!  Junior engineer: Do it, Andrey! Do it for the Motherl...

Mikhalych: Sorry, pal, but I just need it more. You get it, right? You're a machine, so... I need it more. What's yer lot in life? To serve humans, right? Well, I used to serve folks too — I served at Kursk and I served in Berlin. But I didn't do it just to get a fancy medal! I was fightin' for equality, so everybody could have the same rights and responsibilities! So everybody could be like everybody else! Now I just need to figure out how to put your damn thing on...

Junior Roboticist: Hey Mikhail, there's something wrong with the repair vendor in the building over by the drainage pipe. I asked it for a toolbox, but instead of that, a crazy Bumblebee flew out and tossed me a huge container. I can't even get inside it. Go check it out, okay? Nobody else is returning my ca...

Young student: You're incredible, Professor! Your calculations and solutions are so elegant and logical! Your work on mimetic Polymer adaptation is an amazing contribution to science.  Zakharov: Thank you very much, but it was really a team effort... I'm sorry, who are you?  Bykov: Ivan Bykov, junior lab assistant at the Pavlov Complex. I work in the archives, but my dream is to work under you. I'm a huge fan of your work.  Zakharov: Well, your passion is commendable, although it is frankly a little concerning. The Polymers are a quickly evolving scientific field with amazing potential, but I'm afraid passion alone won't be enough to advance it. Let's talk again in a month or so and see what we can do. For now, please excuse me — science calls.  Bykov: A month?! But... I don't have a month. You'll hear about me, Professor! You can bet on it!

Molotov: The sacrifices are worth it. History will vindicate us. Kollektiv is an important step toward something bigger than communism or socialism if the great leaders may forgive me. It's a step toward trans-humanism, the corporation of the future!

Molotov: Famous electronic videogame developer Sergey Suponev... is registering yet another entertainment device! He has made us proud! So we, the Politburo, are putting him up for an award! People like Comrade Suponev are teaching Soviet children the art of happy childhood! That's fine. Type it up, Marina.

(sounds of death)

Get back to me when you can. I'm a little freaked out about this.

VDNH guard: I told you disconnecting the Tereshkovas from the network was a bad idea! They've been acting weird lately. You don't believe me... just listen to this!  Tereshkova: Look, my dearest Claire. See that group of humans? They're visitors. The little ones are newer models. They're called ""children,"" and they make things prettier and more fun. The ones that are a little older are called students. They can do a little bit more. And the older model behind that column is called a ""senior citizen."" And he seems to keep staring at us...  VDNH guard: They're talking about me! They saw me! Those robots were watching the people at the exhibit like they were the exhibit themselves. It's all really creepy... I'd wipe their memory if I were you.

Hospital patient #1: Damn, him too? Shouldn't we at least try to help him?  Hospital patient #2: There's nothing we can do for him. He sat down by her bed like he was hypnotized, and then he just stayed that way. We're the ones who need help now.  Hospital patient #1: My God... but you're right. Those shots were shit. They were supposed to help, but now I've got five people from the same collective farm on my hands.  Hospital patient #2: Um, Vasiliy... something's... something's wrong with me... call the nurse... argh... my side, my side is on fire! Hurry, hurry, call the nurse already!

Petrov: Listen to me, you brainless mutt. Yes, Agent, this recording is for you. I can hear you banging around in the warehouse. You'll never take me alive, so listen up. You have no idea what's going on here, and...  (sounds of death)

So much blood... everywhere... he'll do whatever it takes to bury it all. Nobody will even give a fuck. Hee hee... am I the only one who's resisting it? The blood on my hands is justified!
